text:
#DantePH Update (as of 5 p.m., 22 July 2025)
The low pressure area east of Aurora developed into tropical depression Dante.
Dante is not seen to make landfall but will enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat through Friday, July 25.
No wind signals are expected to be hoisted.
The enhanced habagat will bring significant rainfall over Luzon and some parts of Visayas.
Up to torrential rains may be expected over Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Metro Manila.
Serious threats of flooding and landslides remain.
Dante was spotted 1,130 km east of Northern Luzon at 4 p.m. Tuesday, with winds of 45 kph and gusts up to 55 kph. It is moving north northwestward at 20 kph.
The disturbance will intensify up to tropical storm strength while moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea.
It may exit the Philippine area of responsibility late Thursday or early Friday.
Meanwhile, the low pressure area near Batanes may either merge with the broader circulation of Dante or cross Extreme Northern Luzon towards the northern West Philippine Sea. #WeatherPatrol | via Ariel Rojas, ABS-CBN News

Heavy rain and floods have not stopped a Filipina entrepreneur in the northern Philippines from continuing with her online live-streaming sales while standing submerged in waist-high waters.
Maica Mendoza took advantage of the floods on Friday, July 25, by showcasing her waders live through an online shopping platform, believing that seeing how her items work in the real-life scenario would boost her sales.
Mendoza’s unique live-selling strategy, which she said started back in 2020, has garnered a steady following of over 32,000 followers on TikTok. She lives in Calumpit, Bulacan, which is prone to floods during typhoon or monsoon seasons.
Typhoon #EmongPH made landfall in the province of Pangasinan early morning Friday and has since weakened to a tropical storm after crossing the mountainous region and exiting the landmass of Luzon.

The bill resetting the December 2025 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) and extending the terms of all village and youth officials is set to be signed by President Bongbong Marcos Jr. on August 12. Read more: https://www.sunstar.com.ph/.../comelec-marcos-to-sign... The Duterte brand of leadership ay isang makapangyarihan at mapagpalayang pamumuno na tunay na nagbago sa takbo ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas. Mula sa pagiging Mayor ng Davao na kilala sa disiplina at tapang, dinala ni Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte ang kanyang malasakit at political will sa buong bansa. Hindi siya natakot harapin ang mga oligarko, sindikato, at mga abusadong opisyal. Tinulungan niya maging ang mga politiko na kalauna’y tumalikod sa kanya, kabilang na ang pamilya Marcos, at sa kanyang panahon, ibinalik sa Libingan ng mga Bayani ang labi ni Marcos Sr., isang makasaysayang hakbang na tinanggihan ng mga naunang administrasyon. Sa ilalim ng kanyang liderato, umusbong ang Build Build Build program na nagpatayo ng libo-libong imprastruktura gaya ng expressways, airports tulad ng Bicol International Airport, daan-daang tulay, bypass roads, flood control projects, at maging ang kauna-unahang subway ng Pilipinas. Tumaas ang suweldo ng mga sundalo, pulis, at guro. Sa gitna ng pandemya, matagumpay na nailunsad ang vaccination rollout, naipanalo ang laban sa kaguluhan, at naipamahagi ang ayuda sa milyon-milyong Pilipino. Nilansag niya ang mga teroristang Maute at Abu Sayyaf sa Marawi, pinamunuan ang rehabilitasyon ng lungsod, at isinulong ang localized peace talks sa mga rebeldeng komunista. Sa pamamagitan ng NTF-ELCAC, libo-libong dating NPA fighters ang sumuko at binigyan ng kabuhayan at bagong buhay, habang tuluyang nanghina ang CPP-NPA-NDF sa ideolohiya at operasyon. Ang giyera kontra droga, bagamat kontrobersyal sa mata ng mga banyaga, ay nagligtas ng libo-libong pamilya mula sa kasamaan ng droga, winasak ang drug laboratories, nahuli ang mga drug lord, at nasamsam ang bilyon-bilyong halaga ng ilegal na droga. Nagpatupad siya ng massive anti-corruption campaign, kung saan libo ang nasuspinde, natanggal, at nasampahan ng kaso, kahit pa sila ay malalapit sa kapangyarihan. Pinirmahan niya ang mga batas tulad ng Universal Health Care Law, Free College Tuition Law, Malasakit Center Act, at pinatupad ang 8888 complaint hotline para mas madali ang pagreklamo ng taumbayan sa tiwaling serbisyo ng gobyerno. Naisabatas ang 10-year validity ng passport, 5 to 10-year driver’s license, at isinulong ang digitization ng government transactions para mas mabilis at episyente ang proseso. Sa larangan ng foreign policy, tumayo siya para sa soberanya ng Pilipinas, hindi siya sunod-sunuran sa Amerika o China. Ipinaglaban niya ang karapatan ng bansa sa West Philippine Sea habang iningatan ang diplomasya. Hindi siya nagpadaig sa International Criminal Court at ipinakita sa buong mundo na ang Pilipinas ay isang malayang bansa. Sa gitna ng lahat ng ito, napababa niya ang krimen, napaamo ang trapiko sa EDSA sa pamamagitan ng Bus Rapid Transit system, napakilos ang PNP at AFP na may disiplina, at muling pinaniwala ang sambayanang Pilipino na posible ang gobyernong may malasakit, aksyon, at tunay na serbisyo. Ang kanyang pamumuno ay hindi tungkol sa pa-pogi, kundi sa konkretong resulta. Si Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte ay hindi lamang naging lider kundi naging alamat, isang simbolo ng tapang, katapatan, at pagmamahal sa bayan na hinding-hindi mabubura sa kasaysayan.

24 HR. LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
Issued at   4:00 AM  AUGUST  02, 2025 
Valid Until 4:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting Northern Luzon. Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
TROPICAL CYCLONE OUTSIDE PAR AS OF 3:00 AM TODAY
TROPICAL DEPRESSION
LOCATION: 1,635 KM EAST NORTHEAST OF EXTREME NORTHERN LUZON (26.8 N-136.5 E)
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS: 55 KPH NEAR THE CENTER
GUSTINESS: UP TO 70 KPH
MOVEMENT: NORTHEASTWARD AT 25 KPH
FORECAST:
Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate wind coming from the  Southeast to Southwest  will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to moderate.
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Dakbayan sa Davao ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag um sa kalangitan inubanan sa PAT AK PAT AK  nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms.  Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa  Habagatan Sidlakan ngadto sa Habagatan Kasadpan nga direksyon ang mopasulabi, ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 2.1 meters)
OVER DAVAO CITY:
Temperature  Today:   26˚C to 33˚C
Sunrise (Sidlak)  Today:    5:35 AM
Sunset  (Salop)   Today:   6:00 PM
(gvjr)

text:
WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?

text_content: where is the president now? while typhoon crising lashes the philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and filipinos crying for help, our president is abroad—comfortably meeting with the us president. this is leadership? in the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. no direct presence, no leadership on the ground. just silence. is this the kind of leader we deserve? under the 1987 philippine constitution, the president is the commander-in-chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties. legal basis: article vii, section 4 – the president shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people. article xi, section 1 – public officers, including the president, must at all times be accountable to the people. article xi, section 2 – the president may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty. abandoning the nation during a declared state of calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust. is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? वाराणसी बाढ़ अपडेट | अस्सी घाट और रविदास पार्क का भयावह हाल 
अस्सी घाट और रविदास क्षेत्र में बाढ़ का कहर अब खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंच चुका है।
गंगा नदी का पानी अब सड़कों तक आ गया है, जिससे आम जनजीवन बुरी तरह प्रभावित हो रहा है।
रविदास घाट के आसपास के इलाके पूरी तरह जलमग्न हो चुके हैं, और अस्सी घाट की सीढ़ियां अब गंगा में डूब चुकी हैं।
 रास्ते बंद, दुकानों में पानी, लोगों की आवाजाही ठप
 निचले इलाकों से लोगों का पलायन शुरू
 स्थानीय प्रशासन अलर्ट पर, मगर हालात गंभीर
 अपील है कि अस्सी घाट और आसपास के इलाकों में बिना जरूरत के न जाएं।

ISSUED AT 5:00 AM AUGUST 04, 2025
Valid Until 5:00 AM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS: 
Southwest Monsoon affecting Extreme Northern Luzon.
Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the Southeast to Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 2.5 meters wave height)

Ang Dakbayan sa DAVAO ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati  sa  panalagsa nga pagdag.um ngadto sa mapanganurun nga  kalangitan inubanan sa PAT-AK PAT-AK  nga  pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod  sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang mga pagbaha og landslides kung dunay kusog nga pag ulan.

(0.6 to 2.5 meters wave height).

WATCH: The House of Representatives began on Monday, August 4, its formal review of flood control programs, after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. promised a crackdown on government officials and private sector accomplices that were corrupting such projects.
Bicol Saro Representative Terry Ridon, who presided over the first hearing of the public accounts committee, (1) directed the Department of Public Works and Highways to submit to the House a list of all flood control projects in the last three years, (2) asked the Regional Project Monitoring Committee to submit to the House a list of failed and ghost projects, (3) and promised to publish the list. ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 05 AUGUST2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 PM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA) was estimated based on all available data at 570 km East of Virac, Catanduanes (14.4°N, 129.4°E). Southwest Monsoon affecting Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 2.1 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa patak patak nga pag-ulan kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Possible pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpan direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 2.1 meters).

Depensa ng Palayso, kailangan imbestigahan nang maigi ang mga sinasabing sangkot bago itio isapubliko.

text:
DALAWANG LPA SA LOOB AT LABAS NG PAR, PATULOY NGAYONG BINABANTAYAN 
Ang unang LPA (08a) na nasa silangan ng #Quezon ay patuloy na kumikilos papalapit sa landmass ng #Luzon. Inaasahang tuluyan na itong magla-landfall bukas ng gabi at inaasahang tatawirin ang kalupaan ng #NorthernLuzon hanggang sa Biyernes ng umaga.
Inaasahang bahagya rin nitong hahatakin ang #Habagat na inaasahang magdadala ng mga kalat-kalat na pag-ulan sa bansa partikular sa kanlurang bahagi.
Samantala, isa pang panibagong LPA (08b) ang nabuo sa labas ng PAR o sa silangan ng #NorthernLuzon at may tsansang pumasok ng PAR at maging bagyo sa mga susunod na araw. 
Sakaling maging bagyo ito pagpasok ng PAR, tatawagin itong #FabianPH.
Patuloy na babantayan ang magiging kilos nito dahil hindi rin inaalis ang posibilidad na lumapit ito sa #NorthernLuzon next week.
Manatiling mag-antabay ng mga susunod pang update hinggil sa mga nasabing sama ng panahon sa mga susunod na araw.
— PWS/PSU

SYNOPSIS:
Localized Thunderstorms affecting Mindanao.
TC Information
TROPICAL CYCLONE OUTSIDE PAR AS OF 3:00 AM TODAY
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM PODUL (2511)
LOCATION: 1,875 KM EAST OF EXTREME NORTHERN LUZON (21.5°N, 139.9°E)
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS: 110 KM/H NEAR THE CENTER
GUSTINESS: UP TO 135 KM/H
MOVEMENT: WESTWARD AT 15 KM/H
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from southwest to south with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5meters).

Ang tibuok Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pag dag um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan, inubanan sa patak-patak nga pag ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Possible ang pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin ang maga gikan sa habagatang kasadpan ngadto sa habagatang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto na sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.5 meters)

24 HR. LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
ISSUED AT 5:00 AM AUGUST 11, 2025
Valid Until 5:00 AM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS: 
At 3:00 AM today, the center of Severe Tropical Storm "GORIO" {PODUL} was estimated based on all available data at 1,325 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (21.1°N, 134.6°E) with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 135 km/h. It is moving Westward at 25 km/h.
Southwest Monsoon affecting Western section of Luzon.
Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the South to Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 1.5 meters wave height)
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Dakbayan sa DAVAO ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati  sa  panalagsa nga pagdag.um ngadto sa mapanganurun nga  kalangitan inubanan sa PAT-AK PAT-AK  nga  pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod  sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang mga pagbaha og landslides kung dunay kusog nga pag ulan. 
Hinay ngadto sa Kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa  Habagatan ngadto sa Habagatang Kasadpan nga  direksyon ang mupasulabi, ug ang kadagatan mahimong hapsay ngadto sa  kasarangan ang balod. 
(0.6 to 1.5 meters wave height).

Sunrise (Sidlak)  Today:        5:35 AM

SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 AM today, the center of Typhoon "GORIO" {PODUL} was estimated based on all available data at 755 km East of Itbayat, Batanes (20.7°N, 129.1°E) with maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 150 km/h. It is moving West at 25 km/h
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have Cloudy skies with scattered rainshowers and thunderstorms due to Southwest monsoon. Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms.

Posible ang pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin ang maga gikan sa habagatang kasadpang ngadto sa amihanang kasadpang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto na sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.2 meters).

MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 AM 13 August 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS:
At 3:00 AM today, the center of the eye of Typhoon "GORIO" {PODUL} was estimated based on all available data at 190 km Northeast of Itbayat, Batanes (21.9N, 123.2E) with maximum sustained winds of 140 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 170 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 25 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting the western sections Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM, and SOCCSKSARGEN will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possibe flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstoms. Light to moderate winds from Southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM ug SOCCSKSARGEN makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Samtang ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

বাংলাদেশে বড় বন্যা হতে চলেছে! 
২০২৫ সালের আগস্ট-সেপ্টেম্বর মাসে দেশের ৩০টি জেলায় ভয়াবহ বন্যার সতর্কতা জারি হয়েছে

24-HOUR LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
Issued at 5:00 PM AUGUST 13, 2025
Valid Until 5:00 PM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS:
At 3:00 PM today, the center of the eye of Typhoon "GORIO" {PODUL} was estimated based on all available data at 305 km North Northwest of Itbayat, Batanes (23.1°N, 120.3°E) with maximum sustained winds of 140 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 230 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 25 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting DAVAO REGION and the rest  country. 
FORECAST:  
Davao Oriental will have a cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains.  The rest of Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorm. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds coming from Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to  moderate.
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN: 
Ang Davao Oriental makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Ang nahibiling dapit sa Rehiyon sa Dabaw makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag-um inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan o kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Localized Thunderstorm. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga severe thunderstorms o grabe na pag-ulan. Hinay ngadto sa Kasarangan nga hangin nga magagikan sa Habagatan-Kasadpan nga direksyon ang mopasulabi, ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

Issued at   4:00 AM  AUGUST  14, 2025 
Valid Until 4:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting the country. Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
TROPICAL CYCLONE OUTSIDE PAR AS OF 3:00 AM TODAY
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM PODUL(2511) (FORMERLY  “GORIO”)
LOCATION: 650 KM NORTHWEST OF EXTREME NORTHERN LUZON (24.3 N-116.8 E)
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS: 95 KPH NEAR THE CENTER
GUSTINESS: UP TO160 KPH
MOVEMENT: WEST NORTHWESTWARD AT 35 KPH
FORECAST:
Davao Oriental will experience cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate wind coming from the Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to moderate.
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Davao Oriental makasinati ug madag umun nga kalangitan inubanan sa KATAG KATAG nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Southwest Monsoon O Hangin Habagat. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga kasarangan ngadto sa kusug nga pag ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag um sa kalangitan inubanan sa PAT AK PAT AK  nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa Habagatan Kasadpan nga direksyon ang mopasulabi, ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.5 meters)
OVER DAVAO CITY:

Nag-atubang og daghang warrants of arrest sa Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 10 sa siyudad sa Davao ang kanhing pulis nga si Arturo Lascañas tungod sa mga kasong online libel, murder, ug attempted murder.
Labing uwahing warrant ni Lascañas mao ang online libel pinetsahan Hunyo 9, 2025 nga may pyansang P48,000.
Mga una niyang warrants, mao ang tungod sa kasong murder, pinetsahan Oktubre 16, 2020 nga wa’y pyansa. Laing kaso mai ang attempted murder nga may bail nga P120,000.
Sa maong mga warrants, ang mga otoridad, gimanduan nga ipatuman kini sud sa 10 ka adlaw ug kinahanglang may pagpasabot kung ugaling mapakyas sa pagpatuman ang mga hingtungdan.
Ang mga warrants, naka-address sa mga posibleng gipuy-an ni Lascañas sa Bariquit Compound, Sitio San Andres, Brgy. Indangan, Davao City ug Roseville Subdivision, Buhangin, Davao City.
Kahinumduman nga si Lascañas, mipasiatab nga miyembro siya sa Davao Death Squad, ug alegasyong misibat pagawas sa nasud ug mitestigo batok former President Rodrigo Duterte.

MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 15 August 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting Zamboanga Peninsula. Localized Thunderstorms affecting rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will be partly cloudy to cloudy with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from south to southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang ngadto sa habagatang kasadpang nga direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

text: मुंबईत काल रात्रीपासून मुसळधार पावसाला सुरुवात झाली असून, आजही पावसाचा जोर कायम आहे. अनेक सखल भागांमध्ये पाणी साचले आहे. कुर्ला, विद्याविहार, सायन, दादर किंग सर्कल, चेंबूर, अंधेरी सबवे आणि वाशी मार्केट परिसरात पाणी साचल्याने जनजीवन विस्कळीत झाले आहे. रेल्वे वाहतूकही काही प्रमाणात मंदावली आहे. मुंबई, ठाणे आणि पालघर जिल्ह्यांसाठी ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी करण्यात आला आहे, तर रायगडमध्ये काही ठिकाणी अतिवृष्टीची शक्यता वर्तवण्यात आली आहे. पुणे, सातारा आणि कोल्हापूरच्या घाट परिसरामध्येही जोरदार पावसाचा इशारा देण्यात आला आहे. पुढील तीन दिवस कोकण, मध्य महाराष्ट्र आणि विदर्भात चांगल्या पावसाचा अंदाज आहे. प्रशासनाने नागरिकांना आवश्यक नसल्यास घराबाहेर न पडण्याचे आणि बाहेर पडताना काळजी घेण्याचे आवाहन केले आहे. अमरावती जिल्ह्यातील चांदूर बाजार तालुक्यात झालेल्या पावसामुळे शेतीचे मोठे नुकसान झाले आहे. संत्र्याची झाडे कोसळली असून फळांची गळती झाली आहे. उत्तर रत्नागिरीतील चिपळूण आणि चिंच नाग परिसरातही पाणी साचले असून नद्यांच्या पाणीपातळीत वाढ झाली आहे. या पावसाच्या वातावरणातही राज्यभरात दहिहंडीचा उत्सव उत्साहात साजरा होत आहे. मुंबईतील इस्कॉन मंदिर, ठाण्यातील संकल्प प्रतिष्ठान आणि बदलापूर येथील राधाकृष्ण मंदिरात कृष्ण जन्माष्टमीचा सोहळा साजरा झाला. #MumbaiRains #MaharashtraRains #HeavyRainfall SYNOPSIS: Localized Thunderstorms affecting rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from south to southeast with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. اسلام آباد: خیبر پختونخوا میں گزشتہ 6 گھنٹوں کے دوران بارشوں اور سیلاب سے حادثات میں 145 افراد جاں بحق اور 137 زخمی ہوگئے۔ این ڈی ایم اے کے مطابق ملک بھر میں 6 گھنٹوں میں بارشوں اور سیلابی واقعات سے 151 افراد جاں بحق اور درجنوں زخمی ہوئے جبکہ گزشتہ 48 گھنٹوں میں ہلاکتوں کی تعداد 344 تک پہنچ گئی ہے۔ شمالی علاقوں میں لینڈ سلائیڈنگ کا خدشہ ظاہر کیا گیا ہے اور سیاحوں کو آئندہ چند دنوں تک سفر سے گریز کی ہدایت دی گئی ہے۔ پاک فوج سمیت امدادی ادارے متاثرہ علاقوں میں ریسکیو اور ریلیف سرگرمیوں میں مصروف ہیں، متاثرین کو محفوظ مقامات پر منتقل کیا جارہا ہے۔ پی ڈی ایم اے کے مطابق خیبر پختونخوا کے مختلف اضلاع میں 74 گھروں کو نقصان پہنچا جن میں 11 مکمل طور پر تباہ ہوئے جبکہ متاثرہ اضلاع کے لیے 50 کروڑ روپے جاری کیے گئے ہیں۔ بونیر میں سب سے زیادہ 159 ہلاکتیں رپورٹ ہوئیں جبکہ باجوڑ، بٹگرام اور مانسہرہ میں بھی جانی نقصان ہوا ہے۔ دوسری جانب گلگت بلتستان میں بھی بارشوں اور سیلاب سے تباہی کا سلسلہ جاری ہے جہاں درجنوں افراد جاں بحق، زخمی اور لاپتا ہیں۔

24 HR. LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
ISSUED AT 5:00 PM AUGUST 16, 2025
Valid Until 5:00 PM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS:
Trough of a Low Pressure Area (LPA) affecting Northern and Central Luzon. Southwest Monsoon affecting Southern Luzon and the western section of Visayas. 
LOCALIZED THUNDERSTORMS affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due LOCALIZED THUNDERSTORMS. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the South to Southeast will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 1.8 meters wave height)
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Dakbayan sa DAVAO ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati  sa  panalagsa nga pagdag.um ngadto sa mapanganurun nga  kalangitan inubanan sa PAT-AK PAT-AK  nga  pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod  sa LOCALIZED THUNDERSTORMS. Posible ang mga pagbaha og landslides kung dunay kusog nga pag ulan. 
Hinay ngadto sa Kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa Habagatan ngadto sa Habagatang Sidlakan nga  direksyon ang mupasulabi, ug ang kadagatan mahimong hapsay ngadto sa  kasarangan ang balod. 
(0.6 to 1.8 meters wave height).

Sunrise  (Sidlak)  Tomorrow:   5: 35 AM

Sa kanyang ikaapat na SONA, ipinagmalaki ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” R. Marcos, Jr. ang makabagong teknolohiya ng ating proyekto bilang epektibong bahagi ng disaster awareness at resilience sa tulong ng ating early warning system for landslides.
Ayon naman kay DOST Secretary Renato U. Solidum, Jr., hindi lang teknolohiya ang mahalaga kundi pati na rin ang malaking papel ng komunidad sa paggamit nito at pagsisiguro ng kanilang kaligtasan laban sa anumang panganib.
Patunay nito ang people-centered early warning system na 12 taon nang ipinapatupad ng proyekto, katuwang ang mga lokal na pamahalaan, pamayanan, at iba’t ibang ahensya sa buong bansa.
𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗯𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘁 𝗸𝗼𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗱 𝗻𝗮 𝗻𝗮𝘀𝗮 𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗿𝗼. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗯𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗵𝗮𝘆.
Patuloy na maglilingkod ang 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝘀𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁 para sa inyo 24/7. Gaya ng paalala ng ating Pangulo, “Hindi tayo dapat tumigil sa ating mga ginagawang paghahanda, dahil ang banta ay patuloy na naririyan.”

Southwest Monsoon affecting the western section of Southern Luzon.
Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the Southeast to Northeast will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 1.2 meters wave height)

Ang Dakbayan sa DAVAO ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati  sa  panalagsa nga pagdag.um ngadto sa mapanganurun nga  kalangitan inubanan sa PAT-AK PAT-AK  nga  pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod  sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang mga pagbaha og landslides kung dunay kusog nga pag ulan.

Light to moderate winds from East to Northeast with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.2 meters).

Contractors for flood control projects across the Philippines appeared before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee on Tuesday, August 19, 2025, for a probe into the nation’s flood management issues.
Alan Quirante of QM Builders, a Cebu-based development firm, was among the seven contractors who attended the inquiry. Four other contractors sent representatives, while seven more were absent but submitted written replies.
The Senate hearing followed a report from the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), released on August 11, which ranked Cebu second nationwide in the number of flood control projects despite not being among the country’s top 10 flood-prone provinces.
Based on the National Adaptation Plan of the Philippines 2023–2050, Cebu recorded 414 completed and ongoing flood control projects between July 2022 and May 2025 -- second only to Bulacan. Nationwide, a total of 9,855 projects are in place, amounting to more than P545 billion.
QM Builders is currently ranked as the country’s fourth-largest contractor. The PCO report stemmed from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive during his June 28, 2025, State of the Nation Address. | via SunStar Cebu

text:
BINABANTAYANG LPA SA PACIFIC OCEAN, NAGBABADYA NANG PUMASOK NG PAR BUKAS 
Matapos lumabas ng PAR kaninang umaga ang Tropical Depression #HuaningPH na ngayo’y papalapit na sa #Japan, nagbabadya namang pumasok ng PAR bukas ang isa pang LPA na patuloy na binabantayan.
Hindi inaalis ang tsansa na lumakas ito bilang bagyo at inaasahang lalapit at tatawid ng #NorthernLuzon o #CentralLuzon sa weekend.
Sakaling maging bagyo, tatawagin itong #IsangPH.
Inaasahang bahagya rin nitong hahatakin ang #Habagat na muling magdadala ng kalat-kalat na pag-ulan partikular sa kanlurang bahagi ng bansa sa mga susunod na araw.
Samantala, isa pang kumpol ng kaulapan ang nabuo sa Pacific Ocean na posibleng maging bagong sama ng panahon o LPA sa mga susunod na araw at patuloy na babantayan.
Manatiling mag-monitor ng mga susunod na update hinggil sa nasabing mga weather system dahil posible pa rin ang mga pagbabago rito.
— PWS/PSU

Flood control needs 4R - Responsibility, Reform, Restoration, and Results. Politicians, contractors, and citizens must be accountable—budgets and projects must be published, and corrupt officials jailed. Reform – Educate communities on waste segregation, disaster preparedness, and discipline to prevent flooding. 3. Restoration – Reforest watersheds, plant trees, protect rivers, wetlands, and coastlines, and enforce environmental laws. 4. Results – Ensure transparency, monitor projects, and measure success in reduced flooding, healthier ecosystems, and resilient communities.

text: पुणे (Pune) आणि सातारा (Satara) जिल्ह्यांमध्ये पावसानं विश्रांती घेतल्यामुळे पूरग्रस्तांसाठी दिलासादायक बातमी आहे. उजनी (Ujani) आणि वीर (Veer) धरणाकडे (Dam) येणारा पाण्याचा प्रवाह (Water flow) कमी झाला आहे. यामुळे महापुराचा (Major flood) धोका कमी झाला असला तरी, पुढील दोन दिवस पूरस्थिती (Flood situation) कायम राहील. काल चंद्रभागेच्या (Chandrabhaga) पात्रात जवळपास दीड लाख क्युसेक्स विसर्गानं (Discharge) पाणी वाहत होतं. आज सकाळपर्यंत हा विसर्ग जवळपास एक लाख नव्वद हजार क्युसेक्स पर्यंत पोहोचला आहे. संभाव्य बाधित होणाऱ्या जवळपास दीडशे कुटुंबियांचे (Families) प्रशासनानं (Administration) स्थलांतर (Relocation) केलेलं आहे. प्रशासनाकडून परिस्थितीवर बारीक लक्ष ठेवले जात आहे. #MaharashtraFloods #PuneFloods #SataraFloods #UjaniDam #VeerDam #ChandrabhagaRiver #FloodAlert #RainUpdate #WaterLevel #Evacuation #DisasterManagement #MaharashtraNews #ABP #FloodSituation #Monsoon #IndiaNews पुणे (Pune) आणि सातारा (Satara) जिल्ह्यांमध्ये पावसानं विश्रांती घेतल्यामुळे पूरग्रस्तांसाठी दिलासादायक बातमी आहे. उजनी (Ujani) आणि वीर (Veer) धरणाकडे (Dam) येणारा पाण्याचा प्रवाह (Water flow) कमी झाला आहे. यामुळे महापुराचा (Major flood) धोका कमी झाला असला तरी, पुढील दोन दिवस पूरस्थिती (Flood situation) कायम राहील. काल चंद्रभागेच्या (Chandrabhaga) पात्रात जवळपास दीड लाख क्युसेक्स विसर्गानं (Discharge) पाणी वाहत होतं. आज सकाळपर्यंत हा विसर्ग जवळपास एक लाख नव्वद हजार क्युसेक्स पर्यंत पोहोचला आहे. संभाव्य बाधित होणाऱ्या जवळपास दीडशे कुटुंबियांचे (Families) प्रशासनानं (Administration) स्थलांतर (Relocation) केलेलं आहे. प्रशासनाकडून परिस्थितीवर बारीक लक्ष ठेवले जात आहे. #MaharashtraFloods #PuneFloods #SataraFloods #UjaniDam #VeerDam #ChandrabhagaRiver #FloodAlert #RainUpdate #WaterLevel #Evacuation #DisasterManagement #MaharashtraNews #ABP #FloodSituation #Monsoon #IndiaNews

ISANG MAKES LANDFALL! 
The low-pressure area east of Aurora has intensified into a tropical storm and was officially named #IsangPH by PAGASA.
The storm is expected to cross the Northern and Central Luzon landmass today, bringing heavy rains and strong winds across the region, including Metro Manila.
It will also enhance the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), dumping rains over the western sections of Luzon and the Visayas this weekend.
Authorities warn of possible flash floods and landslides—stay alert and prepared.

LOOK: RDRRMC1 PREPARES FOR #ISANGPH, CONDUCTS PDRA AND WEATHER UPDATING
In anticipation of the possible effects of the Tropical Depression (TD) #ISANGPH in Region I, the Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council 1 (RDRRMC1) convened on 21 August 2025 for a Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA) Scenario Building.
Further, on 22 August 2025, the council also convened for a weather updating to monitor the track and possible effects of TD #ISANGPH. DOST-PAGASA presented the weather forecast and dam updates, while DENR-MGB shared the landslide and flood susceptibility updates.
As of DOST-PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Bulletin No. 1, Tropical Cyclone Warning Signal (TCWS) No. 1 is raised for the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Pangasinan. While based on the Weather Advisory No. 4, heavy rainfall is expected in the provinces of La Union and Pangasinan.
Moreover, based on the DENR-MGB R1, a total of 896 barangays across the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Pangasinan are susceptible to landslide and flooding. 
With the possible effects of TD #ISANGPH, the RDRRMC1 member-agencies and the PDRRMCs of Region I are prepared and ready to respond to any eventualities that may occur.

MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 22 August 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 PM today, the center of Tropical Depression "ISANG" was estimated based on all available data in the vicinity of Maddela, Quirino (16.4N, 121.8E), with maximum sustained winds of 55 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 90 km/h. It is moving West northwestward at 15 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from west to northwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Possible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa kasadpan ngadto na sa amihanang kasadpang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

DOST-PAGASA S & T Media Service
Quezon City, 26 August 2025
LA NIÑA WATCH
LOOMING LA NIÑA CONDITIONS
DOST-PAGASA has been continuously monitoring the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the tropical Pacific. ENSO-neutral is most likely to persist until the August-September-October 2025 season. However, model forecasts suggest an increasing probability of short-lived La Niña conditions as early as the September-October-November season until the October-November-December season.  
La Niña (cool phase of ENSO) is characterized by unusually cooler-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.  When conditions are favorable for the development of La Niña within the next six months and the probability is 55% or more, a La Niña Watch is issued.  
Historically, La Niña is characterized by an above-average number of tropical cyclone occurrences towards the end of the year and above-normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country that can trigger adverse impacts, including floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. 
DOST-PAGASA will continue to closely monitor the possibility of La Niña conditions and its effect on the local climate. All concerned agencies and the public are encouraged to continue monitoring and take precautionary measures against their potential impacts. 
For more information, please call the Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section (CLIMPS), Climatology and Agrometeorology Division (CAD) at telephone number (02) 8284-0800 local 4920 and 4921 or through email: pagasa.climps@gmail.com.

DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE
Bulletin No. 1 on Combined Effects of Low Pressure Area and Southwest Monsoon
Issued at 12:00 NN, 24 August 2025
DOST-PAGASA SITUATIONER
As of 8:00 AM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA)  located 405km east of Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur has a high potential of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.
The LPA will bring cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over Eastern Visayas, Central Visayas, Caraga, Northern Mindanao, and Davao Region. While the Southwest Monsoon and localized thunderstorms will bring partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms over the rest of the country.
ADVISORY TO FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK
The Department is advising farmers to observe and perform the following, as applicable:
1. Regularly monitor the latest local weather information and updates;
2. Harvest mature crops;
3. Secure seed reserves, planting materials, and other farm inputs in safe and proper storage areas; 
4. Relocate farm machineries, equipment, and other farm tools to higher ground;
5. Secure sufficient feeds and water for the possible relocation of animals; and
6. Clear drainage in irrigation and rice paddies from obstructions to prevent flooding and promote fast drainage of water.
Meanwhile, fisherfolk are advised to:
1. Secure fish cages, fish ponds, and fish stocks. Perform early harvest if needed and    mobilize post-harvest equipment and facilities; 
2. Secure fishing vessels in higher ground; 
3. Plan or dismiss sea travel as potentially rough conditions prevail over affected seaboards; and
4. Coordinate and follow fishing advisories from local authorities. 24 HR. LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
ISSUED AT 4:30 PM AUGUST 26, 2025
Valid Until 4:30 PM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS:
At 3:00 PM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA) was estimated based on all available data over the coastal waters of Mercedes, Camarines Norte (14.1°N, 123.1°E). 
Southwest Monsoon affecting Southern Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. 
Southwest Monsoon affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due Southwest Monsoon. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 1.5 meters wave height)

Ang Dakbayan sa DAVAO ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati  sa  panalagsa nga pagdag.um ngadto sa mapanganurun nga  kalangitan inubanan sa PAT-AK PAT-AK  nga  pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod  sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha og landslides kung dunay kusog nga pag ulan. 
Hinay ngadto sa Kasarangan nga huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa Habagatang Kasadpan nga  direksyon ang mupasulabi, ug ang kadagatan mahimong hapsay ngadto sa  kasarangan ang balod. 
(0.6 to 1.5 meters wave height).

weather advisory, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. it provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of heavy rainfall warnings. since a weather advisory is based on a 24-hour outlook, it should not be used as a basis for class suspensions or other official decisions. northern luzon prsd PANOORIN: Ayon kay Maria Bianca Perez, Head ng Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction Office, nakaranas ng hindi pangkaraniwang lakas ng ulan ang lungsod nitong Sabado, Agosto 30, 2025, dahil sa localized thunderstorm.
Umabot sa 141 millimeters ng ulan ang bumuhos sa loob ng isang oras—mas marami pa kaysa sa ulang dala ng bagyong Ondoy noong 2009—na hindi kinaya ng drainage system.
Mahigit 36 barangays ang binaha at nagdulot ng matinding trapiko noong Sabado ng hapon.
Prayoridad ngayon ng lungsod ang pagpapatupad ng Drainage Masterplan, kabilang ang pagpapalawak ng mga drainage system upang makasabay sa urban development at mas matitinding pag-ulan. Issued at:   4:00 PM SEPTEMBER 02, 2025 
Valid Until: 4:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: 
At 3:00 PM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA) was estimated based on all available at 1,170 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (20.2°N, 132.6°E). Southwest Monsoon affecting Southern Luzon and the western section of Visayas.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Organized by the College of Science Student Council, the event aimed "to call for accountability amidst revelations of corruption in government-contracted flood control projects."

Progressive groups staged a mobilization in front of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Region XI office to express their condemnation of anomalies and corruption in the agency's flood control projects, today, September 5.
Notable contractors involved in flood control projects in Davao City include RELY Construction and Supply Inc. managing 71 projects, Genesis88 Construction Inc. with 67 projects, ABU Construction with 32 projects, and Monolithic Construction & Concrete Products Inc. with 28 projects.

Picket rallies were similarly organized at various DPWH regional offices across the country, reinforcing the demand for government accountability for neglecting communities' access to functional and accessible public facilities.

REP. GARBIN APOLOGIZES AFTER CURSING ON LIVE INTERVIEW 
Ako Bicol Party-list Representative Alfredo Garbin Jr. apologized on Monday, September 8, 2025, after a curse word was caught on air during his interview on One Balita Pilipinas.
Garbin explained that he thought the broadcast had already ended when he stumbled while walking, nearly dropped his phone, and blurted out the word.
Earlier in the interview, Garbin said fellow Ako Bicol Representative Zaldy Co is ready to address allegations linking him and his company, Sunwest Construction, to irregularities in flood control projects. Co was mentioned by Curlee Discaya as among those who allegedly received bribes.
Garbin assured he will be more mindful of his words as a public servant and apologized to viewers who may have been offended.

September 19, 2025 - The Office of Civil Defense Region X (OCD X) conducted a site inspection in Valencia City, Bukidnon after a flash flood on September 17, 2025 that affected more than 2,000 families.
OCD X Regional Director and Northern Mindanao Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NorMin RDRRMC) Chairperson Antonio B. Sugarol led the team in coordinating response operations and met with Mayor Amie G. Galario and City DRRM Officer June Ray A. Valero to assess urgent needs.
At the request of the Valencia City LGU, OCD X facilitated the augmentation of three (3) Water Search and Rescue (WASAR) Teams consisting of Special Operations Group of the Philippine Coast Guard, Northern Mindanao, the Cagayan de Oro City DRRMD (CDO-CDRRMD) WASAR Team and 4ID, PA WASAR Team.
In coordination with the Tactical Operations Group 10, Philippine Air Force, two (2) Black Hawk helicopters airlifted the team from 4ID, PA. These teams will augment and assist in the ongoing search and retrieval operations as four (4) persons still remain missing.

 Follow your site’s emergency procedures.

STS “OPONG” affecting Dinagat Islands. Southwest Monsoon affecting the rest Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Dinagat Islands will have rains with gusty winds due to STS OPONG. Possible floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains. Minimal to minor threat to life and property due to strong winds. Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, and rest of Caraga will have occasional rains due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will be partly cloudy to cloudy with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to the southwest monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. The rest of Mindanao will experience moderate to strong winds from southwest with moderate to rough seas (2.5 to 4.0 meters).

Ang Dinagat Islands makasinati sa mga pag ulan ug kalit nga haguros sa hangin tungod kang STS OPONG. Issued at:   4:00 PM SEPTEMBER 25, 2025 
Valid Until: 4:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: 
At 3:00 PM today, the center of Severe Tropical Storm "OPONG" {BUALOI} was estimated based on all available data at 245 km East of Guiuan, Eastern Samar (11.2°N, 128.0°E), with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center and gustiness up to 135 km/h. It is moving Westward at 15 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting Palawan, the rest of Visayas and Mindanao.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Moderate to strong winds from Southwest direction will prevail and the coastal waters will be moderate to rough (2.5  to 4.0 meters Wave Height)

Ang Dakbayan sa Davao ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag-ug ngadto sa madag-umon nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug dalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon o Habagat. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga kusog nga mga pag-ulan. MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 AM 26 September 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 AM today, the center of the eye of Typhoon "OPONG" {BUALOI} was located based on all available data in the vicinity of San Isidro, Northern Samar (12.3°N, 124.4°E), with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center and gustiness up to 150 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 30 km/h. Surigao del Norte and Dinagat Islands affected by TY OPONG. Southwest Monsoon affecting the rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Norte will experience rains with gusty winds due to Typhoon OPONG. Possible floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains to at times intense rains. Minimal to minor threat to life and property due to strong winds. Meanwhile Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao and the rest of Caraga will experience occasional rains due to the Southwest Monsoon. Possible flashfloods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon (Habagat). Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Moderate to Strong winds from the southwest with moderate to rough seas (2.5 to 4.0 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Dinagat Islands ug Surigao del Norte makasinati sa mga pag ulan ug kalit nga huros sa hangin tungod kang TY OPONG. Possible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa kusog ngadto sa usahay intense nga pag-ulan. Samtang ang Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao ug ubang dapit sa CARAGA makasinati sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili say uta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa usahay kusog nga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Kasarangan ngadto sa Kusog nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpang direksyon ug kasarangan ngadto sa baluron nga kadagatan (2.5 to 4.0 meters).

Weather Advisory No. 29
For: Tropical Cyclone OPONG and Southwest Monsoon
Issued at: Sept. 26, 2025, 5 p.m.
Heavy rainfall outlook due to Tropical Cyclone OPONG
Today to tomorrow afternoon (September 27)
(100-200 mm):
Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Romblon, Palawan, and Antique
(50-100 mm):
Metro Manila, Rizal, Bataan, Cavite, Aurora, Isabela, Marinduque, Quezon, Laguna, Batangas, and Aklan
Heavy rainfall outlook due to Southwest Monsoon
Today to tomorrow afternoon (September 27)
Moderate to Heavy (50-100 mm):
Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, Iloilo, Capiz, and Guimaras
Forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas. Moreover, impacts in some areas may be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
The public disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. PAGASA Regional Services Divisions may issue Heavy Rainfall Warnings/Thunderstorm Advisories, and other severe weather information specific to their areas of responsibility as appropriate.
Unless significant changes occur, the next Weather Advisory will be issued at 5:00 AM tomorrow.
𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: The key difference between a 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 and a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 lies in their forecast period, coverage areas, and accuracy. A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬. For class suspensions or other official decisions, please refer to 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 issued by the respective PAGASA Regional Services Divisions.

Officialial Tropical Cyclone Advisory as of 5am, September 26, 2025
SEEK SHELTER NOW! Severe Tropical Storm #OpongPH (BUALOI) is over MASBATE!
Severe Tropical Storm OPONG has slightly weakened but remains a dangerous threat as it traverses the Philippine archipelago. Expect powerful winds, heavy rainfall, and a high risk of life-threatening storm surge.
 TCWS No. 3 in Effect!
Storm-force winds (89-117 km/h) are expected in:
LUZON: Sorsogon, Masbate (including Ticao and Burias Islands), Albay, portions of Camarines Sur/Quezon/Laguna, Marinduque, Romblon, Oriental/Occidental Mindoro, and Batangas.
VISAYAS: Northern Samar, Biliran, and central portions of Eastern Samar, Samar, and Leyte.
Potential Impact: Moderate to significant threat to life and property.
 TCWS No. 2 in Effect!
Gale-force winds (62-88 km/h) expected over:
Metro Manila, the rest of Bicol, Cavite, Rizal, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, and more parts of Southern Luzon and Western Visayas.
Potential Impact: Minor to moderate threat to life and property.
Current Status (5:00 AM, 26 September 2025):
Location: Vicinity of Palanas, Masbate.
Max Winds: 110 km/h | Gustiness: 150 km/h
Movement: West Northwestward at 30 km/h.
 COASTAL HAZARDS: EXTREME RISK!
LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE with peak heights exceeding 3.0 meters is highly possible within 36 hours across low-lying coastal areas of Zambales, Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Mindoro provinces, Bicol Region, and most of Visayas.
Sea Travel is RISKY for ALL TYPES of vessels over the seaboards of Southern Luzon and Visayas due to very rough to very high seas. Mariners must remain in port!
 HEAVY RAINFALL & MONSOON (HABAGAT) ENHANCEMENT:
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 27 for the full rainfall outlook.
The Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), enhanced by Opong, will bring strong to gale-force gusts to areas not under a Wind Signal, including the Ilocos Region, CAR, Cagayan Valley, and Palawan today.
FORECAST: OPONG will continue moving West Northwestward across Masbate, Sibuyan Sea, Southern CALABARZON, and Northern MIMAROPA before exiting to the West Philippine Sea tonight/tomorrow morning.
ACTION ITEMS:
Monitor updates closely. The next bulletin is at 8:00 AM today.
Execute evacuation plans if you are in high-risk zones for storm surge or flooding.
Secure homes and belongings. Do not leave your safety to chance.
SOURCE: DOST

It is moving West Northwestward at 35 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting the western section of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms caused by Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds, variable; with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon/Habagat. Issued at   4:00 AM  September 27, 2025 
Valid Until 4:00 AM Tomorow

It is moving  West Northwestward at 30 kph.  Southwest Monsoon affecting Palawan, Visayas and the western section of  Mindanao.  Localized Thunderstorms  affecting  Davao Region.
FORECAST:
Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds coming from the Northeast to Southeast will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to moderate.

Ang Dakbayan sa Dabaw ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag um  sa kalangitan inubanan sa PAT AK PAT AK  nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Coastal residents, students, and concerned groups staged a protest in Paombong, Bulacan on Saturday, September 27, against alleged anomalous flood control projects in the province.
The town is known to be highly susceptible to flooding.
In an exclusive interview with ABS-CBN News, rallyists said they want government officials implicated in the flood control fiasco held accountable, specifically naming Bulacan 1st District Rep. Danny Domingo and Sen. Joel Villanueva.
The protesters started at Parokya ng Santiago Apostol and they will head to the munincipal office. They advised motorists to take alternates routes as they flooded the streets. | via Ched Gatchalian, ABS-CBN News

WHO NEEDS AIR PATROLS WHEN POLITICIANS HAVE PRIVATE JETS?
Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Jay Tarriela said it was “disheartening” to see a legislator owning multiple air assets while the PCG operates with only three fixed-wing aircraft and two helicopters for maritime patrols.
His statement came after the DPWH asked the AMLC to freeze the air assets of companies linked to Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co, including a Gulfstream jet and several helicopters.
Co is also facing allegations in Senate hearings of inserting billions worth of flood control projects and pocketing kickbacks—including cash allegedly delivered in suitcases—through contractors and engineers. MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 AM 27 September 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 AM today, the center of Typhoon "OPONG" {BUALOI} was estimated based on all available data at 470 km West of Ambulong, Tanauan City, Batangas (14.1_N, 116.7_E), with maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h near the center and gustiness up to 150 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 30 km/h. Southwest Monsoon Zamboanga Peninsula, while Localized Thunderstorms affecting rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms caused by Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds, from the northeast to southeast; with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon/Habagat. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa usahay kusog nga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa mga severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa amihanang silangan ngadto sa habagatang silangan nga diresksyon ug hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan nga kadagatan (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

text:
𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗: Severe Tropical Storm (STS) Opong caused massive destruction as it battered large parts of the Visayas and Bicol Region, leaving at least four people dead and displacing more than 360,000 families, or about 1.414 million individuals, due to flooding and landslides.
In its 11:00 p.m. bulletin, PAGASA reported that STS Opong was located 260 kilometers west of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro, as it moved over the West Philippine Sea. It is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) this morning or by midday, heading toward the northern part of Vietnam with sustained winds of 110 kph and gusts of up to 135 kph.
According to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), more than 87,000 residents in the Bicol Region evacuated, while around 73,000 individuals remain in evacuation centers in Eastern Samar and Northern Samar.
In Masbate, three fatalities were reported, including one crushed by a fallen tree, while another person in Camarines Norte was struck by lightning. Around 20,000 people were affected in Masbate, governor Richard Kho said.
The storm impacted 11 regions, particularly 46 provinces, 391 cities and municipalities, and 2,891 barangays.
Experts have long warned that typhoons are becoming stronger and more frequent due to global warming, resulting in more severe damage to vulnerable communities.
STS Opong struck just days after Super Typhoon Ragasa, which killed at least nine people and displaced thousands in Northern Luzon. The back-to-back disasters have made it more difficult for local governments to provide aid and repair damaged infrastructure.
Meanwhile, as the public struggles with the devastation brought by successive storms, a major controversy surrounds government flood control projects. Investigations suggest that some officials may have profited from multi-billion peso kickbacks, allegedly spent on lavish lifestyles instead of urgently needed infrastructure against disasters. The issue sparked massive protests on September 21, 2025, at Rizal Park in Manila and at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City.
The impact of STS Opong goes beyond the loss of lives and properties, it also highlights the deeper issues the country faces, from the effects of climate change to corruption in projects that should have served as vital defenses against natural calamities.

Ang daming budget na nilamon ng fake projects, ang daming drainage na ginawa para lang may masabing nagawa, tapos laging sira o bara agad. Ang gobyerno, dapat long-term solutions ang iniisip, hindi puro band-aid at photo ops tuwing baha season.
Pero let’s be real, hindi rin tayo malinis. Sino ba talaga ang nagtatapon ng basura sa kalye? Sino ang nagsisiksik ng plastic sa kanal? Sino ang nag-iiwan ng kalat sa ilog? Hindi naman si mayor o si congressman yun. Mga tao rin. Tayo rin.
So yes, the government failed us. Pero wag din natin i-deny, tayo rin may ambag sa problemang ‘to. Kahit gaano kaganda ang drainage na gawin nila, kung tayo pa rin mismo ang bumabara gamit ang sariling kalat, wala ring kwenta.
Truth hurts: Gobyerno + palpak na projects = baha. 
Citizens + walang disiplina = baha. 
Pinagsamang sablay? Guaranteed baha.
Kaya bago tayo magrereklamo, tanungin din natin ang mga sarili natin: "Am I part of the solution, or am I part of the problem?"
SA gobyerno, AYUSIN NYO TRABAHO NYO. SATING MGA CITIZENS, magtapon ng basura ng tama. Kung parehong palpak, wag na tayong magtaka kung lulubog tayo sa sarili nating kalokohan. WE ARE THE FLOOD. 
On a serious note, the government holds the biggest responsibility to protect the people, pero as citizens, may part din tayo. Kung sabay gumalaw ang gobyerno at ang tao, mas may chance pa tayo.

Issued at 5:00 PM SEPTEMBER 28, 2025
Valid Until 5:00 PM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS: Easterlies affecting DAVAO REGION 
FORECAST:  
DAVAO REGION will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to the Easterlies. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from the northeast to southeast with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 2.5 meters).

Almost five days worth of September rain was dumped in Quezon City in just two hours during Monday’s midday downpour, PAGASA data showed.
A total of 82 millimeters of precipitation was recorded at the Science Garden station between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m., September 29, 2025.
The monthly rainfall in Quezon City for September is 500.3 mm.
The weather bureau said an intense thunderstorm affected northern and central Metro Manila and parts of Rizal and Bulacan midday Monday.
On August 30, a cloudburst — high volume precipitation over a small area in a short period of time — occurred in Quezon City and brought almost 100 mm of rain.

MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 30 September 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Easterlies affecting Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to the Easterlies. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from the east to southeast with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Easterlies. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa mga severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa silangan ngadto na sa habagatang silangang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.8 meters).

Nanawagan si Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Remulla kay Zaldy Co na humarap sa mga kasong isinampa laban sa kanya matapos irekomenda ng Independent Commission for Infrastructure ang pagsasampa ng graft at malversation charges kaugnay ng P289.5-milyong flood control project sa Naujan, Oriental Mindoro.
Kasama sa iniimbestigahan si Co at ilang opisyal ng Department of Public Works and Highways na umano’y sangkot sa maanomalyang bidding at overpricing ng proyekto, na pinaniniwalaang nagdulot ng milyon-milyong pisong pagkalugi sa pamahalaan.
 “He has to face the music… Harapin ang mga charges if you say you are innocent,” ani Remulla nitong Lunes, September 29.
Dagdag pa ng kalihim, hihilingin ng DOJ sa Interpol ang pag-isyu ng blue notice para matunton ang kinaroroonan at aktibidad ni Co.

VIETNAM GI IGO SA BAGYO 
Ang kanhi Bagyong Bualoi midasmag sa Central Vietnam
 Daghang Patay, Dakong Kalaglagan Ang kanhing bagyo mi-landfall sa sentro sa Vietnam sayo sa Septembre 29, dayon gisubay sa yuta paingon sa Laos. 
Mga epekto hangtod karon:
 Labing menos 12 ang kompirmadong patay, 17 ang missing 347,000+
ka balay ang nahabilin nga walay kuryente.
 Mga dalan, tulay, eskwelahan naguba 
Ang mga sakayan sa pangisda naanod Ikaduhang mga Risgo:
 Ang padayon nga kusog nga ulan naghulga sa kalit nga pagbaha, pagdahili sa yuta, ug pag-awas sa mga suba sa tibuok Vietnam, Laos, ug sa ubos nga mga rehiyon.
 Mga Tip sa Pagpangandam: Kung naa ka sa lugar nga huyang 
• Pagtuman sa mga mando sa pagbakwit 
• Magpalayo sa mga tampi sa suba 
• Hupti nga andam ang mga suplay sa emerhensya 
• Sunda ang opisyal nga mga panagna ug mga pasidaan Konteksto sa Rehiyon: 
Giguba una sa Bualoi ang Pilipinas, dayon gipakusog una naigo ang Vietnam.
 Gipasidan-an sa mga eksperto nga ang pagbag-o sa klima nagpadako sa kusog nga mga bagyo sa tibuuk nga Asya.
 Ang mga hunahuna anaa sa tanan nga apektado. 
Ang mga paningkamot sa pagtabang nagpadayon.

Tuluyan nang pumasok ng PAR ngayong Martes ng gabi, September 30, ang isang aktibong LPA na patuloy na binabantayan sa silangan ng #BicolRegion.
Base sa mga weather model, mataas na ang tsansa nitong maging bagyo sa loob ng 24-48 oras at nagbabadyang kumilos papalapit sa bahagi ng #NorthernLuzon, at posibleng mag-landfall sa bahagi ng #Cagayan-#Isabela area at tsaka tatawirin ang #NorthernLuzon mula Biyernes hanggang Sabado (Oct. 3-4).
Inaabisuhan ang mga residente maging sa bahagi ng #CentralLuzon na paghandaan ang inaasahang epekto ng papalapit na potensyal na bagyong ito sa mga susunod na araw.
Sakaling lumakas na bilang bagyo habang nasa loob ng PAR, tatawagin itong #PauloPH.
Patuloy na mag-monitor ng mga susunod pang update hinggil dito.

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 1
Tropical Depression #PaoloPH
Issued at 11:00 AM, 01 October 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 5:00 PM today.
THE LOW PRESSURE AREA EAST OF SOUTHERN LUZON DEVELOPED INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION “PAOLO”.
• Location of Center (7:00 AM):
The center of Tropical Depression PAOLO was estimated based on all available data at 760 km East of Virac, Catanduanes (14.1°N, 131.2°E).
• Intensity:
Maximum sustained winds of 45 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 55 km/h, and central pressure of 1004 hPa
• Present Movement:
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong winds extend outwards up to 360 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
 ➣ No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
 ➣ Heavy Rainfall Outlook
PAOLO is less likely to directly affect the weather condition of the country in the next 24 hours. Onset of heavy rains due PAOLO is possible by Friday (03 October) onwards. A weather advisory may be released today in anticipation of the heavy rains that PAOLO may bring over Northern Luzon and portions of Central Luzon.
 ➣ Severe Winds
Wind Signal No. 1 may be hoisted over the eastern sections of Northern and Central Luzon as early as this afternoon or evening. The highest Wind Signal that will likely be hoisted throughout its passage is Wind Signal No. 3. However, since the possibility of reaching typhoon category before landfall is not ruled out, the worst case scenario is Wind Signal No. 4.
 ➣ Coastal Inundation
There is a potential risk of coastal flooding due to storm surge in low-lying coastal areas of Northern and Central Luzon due to the passage of PAOLO. Storm surge warning may be issued today or tomorrow (02 October).
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
 ➣ 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
PAOLO may bring moderate to rough seas over the coastal waters of Northern and Central Luzon starting Friday (03 October) early morning. Gale Warning may be raised over the seaboards of Northern and Central Luzon as early as tomorrow (02 October) afternoon in anticipation of rough to very rough sea conditions. 
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• PAOLO is forecast to move generally west northwestward for the entire forecast period. On the forecast track, PAOLO may make landfall over Isabela or northern Aurora on Friday (03 October) morning or afternoon. Further southward shift of track is possible depending on the strength of the high pressure area to the north of PAOLO.
• PAOLO will continue to intensify while over the Philippine Sea and may reach severe tropical storm category by Friday morning. Further intensification into a Typhoon prior to landfall is not ruled out. 
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
The next tropical cyclone bulletin will be issued at 5:00 PM today.
DOST-PAGASA

24-HOUR LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
Issued at:   4:00 PM OCTOBER 02, 2025 
Valid Until: 4:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: 
At 3:00 PM today, the center of Tropical Storm "PAOLO" {MATMO} was estimated based on all available data at 490 km East of Infanta, Quezon (15.2°N, 126.2°E), with maximum sustained winds of 85 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 105 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 10 km/h.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Moderate winds from southeast to south direction will prevail and the coastal waters will be moderate (1.2  to 2.5 meters Wave Height)
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Dakbayan sa Davao ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag-ug ngadto sa madag-umon nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug dalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Kasarangan nga  huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa habagatang sidlakan ngato sa habagatang direksyon ang mopasulabi, ug ang kadagatan, kasarangan ang pagbalud (1.2 to 2.5 meters Wave Height)
OVER DAVAO CITY:
Temperatura Ugma:        24˚C to 32˚C
Sunset (salop) Karon:     5:32 PM
Sunrise (Sidlak) Ugma:   5:29 AM

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has submitted documents to the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) to freeze the bank accounts of dismissed Department of Public Works and Highways district engineer Henry Alcantara, Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Remulla said on Tuesday.
Alcantara was brought to the DOJ for evaluation on whether he could be placed under the government’s Witness Protection Program (WPP) as part of the ongoing investigation into the anomalous flood-control program.
“That was just the first part. We have to see him (Alcantara) again within the week to finalize everything. But we did good work. We prepared some documents [and] submitted to AMLC the required documents so they could freeze the bank accounts,” Remulla told reporters.

READ: In the wake of the recent magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck northern Cebu, a group of innovative Cebuanos has launched a real-time relief coordination app that is quickly becoming a lifeline for affected communities.
Created by Vince Datanagan, Ralph Dilao, and Clint Alonzo — three students from the University of Cebu – Main Campus, the app allows victims to pin their exact locations and describe their urgent needs, such as food, water, medicine, shelter, and other essentials. Each pin submitted to the map represents not just a location, but a life, a family, and a plea for help.
 Matag pin = usa ka pamilya, usa ka kinabuhi.
Donors, volunteers, LGUs, NGOs ug uban pang grupo makakita sa live requests sa mapa ug dali maka-responde. Ang mga pinned locations nagpakita sa mga urgent needs — pagkaon, tubig, tambal, tabang para sa mga bata, tigulang, ug mga naa sa layo nga lugar.
 I-share kini sa mga volunteers ug kauban nga makatabang.
 Link sa app naa sa comment section.
 Gamiton nato ang platform sa husto — walay spam kay “every pin matters.”

EARTHQUAKE RESPONSE UPDATE | Dagdag 12,700 Food Packs sa mga Apektado ng Lindol sa Cebu
Bilang tugon sa patuloy na pangangailangan ng mga apektadong pamilya, nagpadala ang DSWD ng karagdagang 12,700 kahon ng family food packs (FFPs) sa iba’t ibang bayan sa Cebu na matinding tinamaan ng magnitude 6.9 na lindol.
Kabilang sa nakatakdang padalhan ay ang Borbon (4,000 FFPs), Tabuelan (2,000 FFPs), Bantayan (2,000 FFPs), Medellin (2,000 FFPs), at Sogod (2,700 FFPs). 
Ngayong Biyernes (Okt. 3), umabot na sa halos 27,100 FFPs ang na-dispatch ng Visayas Disaster Resource Center (VDRC) ng DSWD. 
Ang karagdagang tulong ay bahagi ng 150,000 na kabuuang FFPs na ipapamahagi sa mga lokal na pamahalaan ng Cebu. BAGYONG “PAOLO” MAGDADALA NG MALAKAS NA ULAN SA NUEVA VIZCAYA AT KALAPIT-LUGAR
Nagbabala ang PAGASA na asahan ang matinding pagbuhos ng ulan sa malaking bahagi ng Hilagang Luzon dala ng Severe Tropical Storm “Paolo”. Ayon sa Weather Advisory No. 6 na inilabas nitong Oktubre 2, 2025 alas-11 ng gabi, posibleng umabot sa 100 hanggang 200 milimetro ang ulan bukas hanggang gabi sa Nueva Vizcaya, kasama ang Cagayan, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan at Nueva Ecija. Mas malakas pa ang inaasahang ulan sa Isabela, Quirino at Aurora na maaaring lumampas sa 200 milimetro. Binalaan ng mga eksperto na mas mataas pa ang epekto sa mga kabundukan at matataas na lugar, na posibleng magdulot ng landslide at pagbaha.
Mula bukas ng gabi hanggang Sabado ng gabi, Oktubre 4, patuloy pa rin ang malalakas na ulan sa Ilocos Region, Benguet, Abra, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Zambales at Tarlac. Dahil dito, mahigpit na pinapayuhan ang mga residente at mga lokal na pamahalaan na magsagawa ng agarang paghahanda at sumunod sa mga abiso ng kani-kanilang DRRMO. Ipinaliwanag din ng PAGASA na ang Weather Advisory ay nagbibigay ng mas malawak na tanaw sa loob ng 24 oras, habang ang Heavy Rainfall Warning ay nakatuon sa susunod na tatlong oras gamit ang Doppler radar na mas eksakto para sa mga agarang desisyon tulad ng class suspensions at paglilikas. Ang susunod na abiso ay ilalabas bukas ng alas-5 ng umaga.

24 HR. LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
Issued at   4:00 AM  October  04, 2025 
Valid Until 4:00 AM Tomorow
SYNOPSIS:  At 3:00 AM today, the center of Severe Tropical Storm  “PAOLO” {MATMO} was estimated based on all available data at 200 km West of Sinait, Ilocos Sur (17.9 N- 118.1 E). with maximum sustained winds of 110 kph near the center and gustiness of up to 135 kph. It is moving West Northwestward at 20 kph. Localized Thunderstorms affecting  Davao Region.
FORECAST:
Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds coming from the Northeast to Southeast  will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to moderate.
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN:
Ang Dakbayan sa Dabaw ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati ug panalagsang pagdag um sa kalangitan inubanan sa PAT AK PAT AK  nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga  huyop sa hangin nga magagikan sa Amihanang Sidlakan ngadto sa Habagatan Sidlakan nga direksyon and mopasulabi ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pag balud.(0.6 to 1.5 meters)
OVER DAVAO CITY:
Temperature  Today:   24˚C to 33˚C
Sunrise  (Sidlak) Today:  5:29 AM
Sunset  (Salop)  Today:  5:31 PM

LOOK: A tragedy struck Barangay Bilwang, Kawayan, Biliran on the afternoon of Friday, September 26, 2025, after three family members drowned while another child remains missing.
The fatalities include a 4-year-old girl, a 12-year-old girl, and their 63-year-old grandfather known as “Gil.” Meanwhile, a 7-year-old child has yet to be found.
According to reports, water from a creek suddenly overflowed, causing flooding in their home and leading to their drowning. Their bodies were later recovered and brought to the Bilwang barangay hall.
Search and retrieval operations are still ongoing to locate the missing child.
