MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 04 October 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: At 3:00 PM today, the center of Severe Tropical Storm MATMO {Formerly “PAOLO”} was estimated based on all available data at 570 km West of Sinait, Ilocos Sur (18.4°N, 115.1°E), with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 135 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 20 km/h. Another Topical Depression outside PAR, was estimated based on all available data at 2,285 km East Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (24.3°N, 143.8°E) with maximum sustained winds of 55 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 70 km/h. It is moving North Northwestward at 10 km/h. Localized Thunderstorm affecting Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from northeast to northwest over the eastern sections of Mindanao with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters). Elsewhere, light to moderate winds from southwest to northwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa severe thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin gikan sa amihanang silangan ngadto na sa amihanang kasadpang direksyon ang magpasulabi sa silangang dapit sa Mindanao ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto na sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.5 meters). Samtang ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao, adunay hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin gikan sa habagatang kasadpan ngadto na sa amihanang kasadpang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto na sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

Binigyang-diin ni Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Sec. Amenah F. Pangandaman noong nakaraang Huwebes, ika-25 ng Setyembre na hindi kasali ang kanyang ahensiya sa iskandalong pumapalibot sa mga flood control projects na isinasagawa sa bansa.

Metro Manila and Cebu City, Philippines — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) has deployed an eight-member team of geologists, consisting of six from the Central Office and two from Regional Office VII, to conduct a comprehensive Post-Disaster Geohazards Assessment across several areas in Cebu Province. The assessment aims to identify zones susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, ground subsidence, and sinkhole formation.
The initiative aims to enhance public safety and guide local government units (LGUs) in land-use planning and disaster risk reduction, particularly in communities situated on karst terrains characterized by limestone formations that are prone to dissolution and collapse.
According to Assistant Secretary for Mining Concerns and concurrent OIC Director Engr. Michael V. Cabalda, the assessment involves ground validation and geohazards data analysis. “This study will enable us to pinpoint areas susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, and those areas with high potential for ground subsidence and provide technical recommendations to LGUs for proper zoning, building regulation, and emergency preparedness,” the Engr. Cabalda said.

ALAMIN | 
 𝐁𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐭 𝐧𝐚𝐠-𝐬𝐮𝐥𝐩𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐠𝐚 𝐒𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐬𝐚 𝐍𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐂𝐞𝐛𝐮?
Nakita niyo ba ang mga sinkhole na lumabas matapos ang na lindol noong Setyembre 30? Hindi lang ito simpleng butas sa lupa! May mas malaking geological reason diyan: ang 𝐊𝐀𝐑𝐒𝐓 𝐒𝐔𝐁𝐒𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐄.
𝐀𝐍𝐎 𝐈𝐓𝐎?
1. Limestone Area: Ang Northern Cebu ay isang "karst area," kung saan ang lupa ay mayaman sa limestone (carbonate rock).
2. Natunaw na Bato: Sa loob ng libu-libo o milyun-milyong taon, natutunaw ang limestone, kaya nagkakaroon ng malawak na cave system sa ilalim ng lupa. Nawawalan ng suporta ang lupa sa ibabaw.
3. Lindol ang "Trigger": Ang malakas na lindol ay nag-trigger o nagpabagsak sa mga mahihinang bahagi ng 'bubong' ng cave system, kaya biglang lumabas ang mga sinkhole. Nangyari na rin ito noong 2013 Bohol earthquake!
𝐏𝐎𝐒𝐈𝐁𝐋𝐄 𝐁𝐀𝐍𝐆 𝐌𝐀𝐍𝐆𝐘𝐀𝐑𝐈 𝐒𝐀 𝐋𝐔𝐆𝐀𝐑 𝐌𝐎?
Oo, kung ang lugar mo ay classified din bilang isang karst area.
  𝐌𝐀𝐆𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐇𝐀𝐍𝐃𝐀 𝐀𝐓 𝐌𝐀𝐆-𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐄𝐀𝐑𝐂𝐇!

HOW CAN WE #MAKEPANGASINANLIVEABLE?
Around 134 Pangasinenses gathered on Thursday, October 2, at the Lay Formation Center in Dagupan City for Rappler’s #MakePangasinanLiveable public forum. 
Local officials, community leaders, and citizens came together to talk about urgent concerns in the community, including flooding, education, healthcare, public safety, and good governance, and what can be done together to address them.
The public forum is part of Rappler’s civic empowerment roadshow, “#AmbagNatin: Engage for Change,” which aims to bring people and institutions together to shape better communities from the ground up.
This Pangasinan leg was organized in partnership with the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan and the AB English Language program of Pangasinan State University Lingayen Campus, with food sponsorship by Mang Inasal.

OCCIDENTAL MINDORO– Isang mas malakas na pagyanig ang naitala sa bandang alas-8:54 ng gabi nitong Sabado, Oktubre 5, 2025, matapos ang naunang serye ng maliliit na lindol.
Batay sa ulat ng Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), ang lindol ay may lakas na Magnitude 4.2 at may lalim na 10 kilometro. Ang sentro o epicenter nito ay natukoy 4 na kilometro S 85° W ng Santa Cruz, Occidental Mindoro.
Narito ang naitalang Instrumental Intensities:
III (Weak) Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro; Abra De Ilog, Occidental Mindoro
I (Scarcely Perceptible) Sablayan, Occidental Mindoro at City of Batangas
Ang Intensity III ay karaniwang nararamdaman sa loob ng bahay, lalo na sa itaas na palapag, at maaaring makita ang mga sasakyang nakaparada na umuuga. Samantala, ang Intensity I ay halos hindi nararamdaman.
Ayon sa PHIVOLCS, bagamat may kalakasan ang pagyanig, walang inaasahang pinsala mula rito. Gayunpaman, inaasahan ang mga aftershocks kasunod ng lindol na ito.

 bandang alas-9:07 at alas-9:11 ng gabi.

text:
As rains continue to flood parts of the country, health experts are sounding the alarm on leptospirosis — a serious infection that can be life-threatening if not treated early.
The Pediatric Nephrology Society of the Philippines, a group of local kidney specialists for kids, recently shared tips on how to spot and prevent leptospirosis, especially in children.
What is leptospirosis?
It’s a disease you can get by:
 Wading in floodwater
 Drinking water contaminated with rat urine or waste from other infected animals
 The bacteria (called leptospira) can enter your body through:
Open wounds
Scratches or broken skin soaked in floodwater
 Symptoms to watch out for:
Fever
Headache
Stomach pain
Red eyes
Yellowing of the skin (jaundice)
Trouble peeing
Shortness of breath
 Preventive meds you should know about:
If your child has waded through floodwater even just once, here’s what the experts recommend:
 Doxycycline 100 mg (2 tablets within 24 hours) — available for free at health centers
 Azithromycin (10 mg/kg single dose, max 500 mg)
 Amoxicillin (50 mg/kg/day, every 6 hours for 3–5 days, max 500 mg per dose)
If exposure happened over 7 days ago, they should take medicine again after a week.
OpinYonistas, avoid floodwater if you can.

Ang mga pag-ulang nararanasan sa naturang lugar ay dulot ng umiiral na Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ).

text:
ISANG LALAKI, KUMAPIT SA PUNO NG NIYOG PARA MAILIGTAS ANG BUHAY SA GITNA NG RUMARAGASANG BAHA SA SARANGANI! 
Nakapanlulumong tagpo sa Maasim, #Sarangani, matapos ma-trap ang isang lalaki sa biglaang pagtaas ng tubig-baha dulot ng walang tigil na ulan mula sa Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) nitong Lunes, October 6, 2025.
 Sa gitna ng rumaragasang agos, napilitan siyang kumapit sa puno ng niyog upang hindi matangay ng baha.
Habang humahampas ang tubig, makikita ang matinding takot, tapang, at pag-asang mabuhay sa kanyang ginawa — isang tagpo na sumasalamin sa tibay ng Pilipino sa gitna ng sakuna.

Ang baha ay isa sa mga pinakamalaking problema sa Pilipinas. Ito ay nakapagtataka dahil kilala tayo sa ating mga likas na yaman. Bakit patuloy tayong nakakaranas ng baha?
Ang pangunahing dahilan ay ang korapsyon. Ang mga opisyal at kontraktor ay ninanakaw ang pondo na dapat mapunta sa mga proyekto na makakatulong sa ating kalikasan at sa mga mahihirap, tulad na lamang ng maayos na drainage system at relokasyon sa ligtas na lugar.
Dahil dito, hindi lahat ng Pilipino ay may kakayahang bumangon o makaahon pagkatapos ng sakuna. Maraming nagugutom, nawawalan ng tirahan, at napipilitang mamuhay sa peligro. Bilang isang taong nakakaranas nito, alam ko gaano kahirap ang ganitong karanasan.
Kailangan natin ng pagbabago. Kailangan natin ng mga pinuno na tapat at may malasakit sa pinamumunuan niya. Sama-sama nating labanan ang korapsyon at ipaglaban ang karapatan nating mga PILIPINO.

DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | Kasama ng Masbate ang DSWD sa Muling Pagbangon!
Dalawang linggo matapos ang pananalasa ng Bagyong #OpongPH sa Bicol Region, patuloy ang Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) sa paghahatid ng tulong sa mga Bicolanong naapektuhan at ngayo’y unti-unti nang bumabangon mula sa pinsalang iniwan ng bagyo.
Bilang bahagi ng nagpapatuloy na pagtugon sa Masbate, muling lumipad si DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian sa island province para kumustahin ang kalagayan ng mga apektadong pamilya at alamin ang iba pang tulong na maaaring maiparating ng ahensya.
Sa pagbisita ng Kalihim sa Masbate, nakita niya ang pamamahagi ng DSWD Field Office 5 - Bicol Region ng 500 kahon ng family food packs (FFPs) sa mga residenteng apektado sa Dimasalang, Masbate ngayong Miyerkules (Oktubre 
.
Kasabay nito, nagpapatuloy din sa bayan ang medical mission ng DSWD katuwang ang Provincial Health Office ng Camarines Sur para matulungan ang mga residenteng nangangailangan ng agarang serbisyong medikal. Naka-deploy rin ang mobile kitchen para sa mainit na pagkain at water purifying truck na nagsisiguro sa ligtas at malinis na suplay ng inuming tubig para sa mga residente.
Kasama ni Secretary Gatchalian sa ikatlong biyahe sa Masbate sina Undersecretary Diana Rose Cajipe ng Disaster Response Management Group (DRMG, Field Office 5 Regional Director Norman Laurio, Dimasalang Mayor Michael Demph Naga, at Masbate Governor Ricardo Kho.
Source: Department of Social Welfare and Development - DSWD

The impact of three successive cyclones that hit Luzon in early July 2025 served as a wake-up call for both the public and the government about the grave and seemingly perpetual problem of flooding.
So when perennial flood victim and mountain water catch basin Marikina saw clear streets despite nearby areas being submerged, netizens cannot help but ask what the city did differently.
The answer, Marikina 2nd District Rep. Miro Quimbo said, lies in a 15-year plan that consists of different measures — from improving the area’s waterways, creating new channels for water to flow to rivers, and ensuring that infrastructure projects are attuned to the city’s needs. | via inquirer.net

ISSUED AT: 5:00 AM 09 October 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwesterly Windflow affecting Mindanao.
TC Information
TROPICAL CYCLONE OUTSIDE PAR AS OF 3:00 AM TODAY
TROPICAL STORM {NAKRI} (2523)
LOCATION: 1,505 KM EAST OF EXTREME NORTHERN LUZON (21.9N, 136.3E)
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS: 65 KM/H NEAR THE CENTER
GUSTINESS: UP TO 80 KM/H
MOVEMENT: NORTHWESTWARD AT 25 KM/H
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwesterly Windflow. Possible flashfloods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. Light to moderate winds prevail from southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang tibuok dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwesterly Windflow. Posible ang pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpang direksyon, ug ang kadagatan, hapsay ngadto na sa kasarangan ang pagbalud (0.6 to 1.8 meters).

FLASHFLOOD, NAMERWISYO SA MAASIM, SARANGANI PROVINCE 
Rumaragasang tubig-baha na may kasamang putik at mga debris ang dumaloy sa bahagi ng National Highway sakop ng Tinago, Brgy. Poblacion, Maasim, #Sarangani nitong Lunes ng hapon, October 6, 2025.
Ayon sa mga residente, umapaw ang Tinago Creek matapos itong mabarahan ng mga putol na sanga at iba pang debris mula sa bundok dahilan upang tuluyang umapaw at rumagasa ang tubig-baha sa kalsada.
Wala namang napaulat na nasugatan sa biglaang pagbaha ayon sa kanilang MDRRMO.
Ang mga pag-ulang nararanasan sa naturang lugar ay dulot ng umiiral na Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ).
 Brian Ruselle Borja

ICYMI: The 2nd day of GeoRiskPH for Resilience Regional Training, implemented by DOST-PHIVOLCS and the DRREALL-TA Project, continued to relay practical skills and knowledge on Disaster Risk Management to the participating local government units and learning resource institutes yesterday, October 8, 2025 at Richmonde Hotel, Eastwood City, Quezon City.
Ms. Gizella Marie Herrera, Project Coordinator of Agence Française de Développement (AFD) Philippines Country Office, delivered a message to the participants. Meanwhile, Dr. Marqueza L. Reyes of Expertise France lectured on Disaster Risk Management Framework and Aspects.
DOST-PHIVOLCS led a lecture on Earthquake and Volcanic Hazards while the Department of Environment and Natural Resources - Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) discussed the Flooding and Landslide Hazards and DOST- Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) shared insights on Weather and Climate Hazards.
Also, DOST-PHIVOLCS taught the participants on the GeoRiskPh Platforms as well as utilizing these technologies to generate risk assessment and local planning processes which foster best practices in the implementation of GeoRiskPH.
Ms. Joan C. Salcedo of DOST-PHIVOLCS delivered the closing message, thanking the organizers and partner agencies in championing activities that demonstrate the progress and advancements made in GeoRiskPH and gather feedback from end-users and stakeholders.
#GeoRiskPH #OneDOST4U #SolutionsAndOpportunitiesforAll

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority and Valenzuela City government conducted cleanup operations on the Meycauayan River on Thursday as part of the Bayanihan sa Estero program to clear waterways of trash and silt and prevent flooding.
The cleanup, done with backhoes mounted on barges, was carried out in Barangay Caingin on the boundary of Valenzuela City and Meycauayan, Bulacan.
"Malaki ang maitutulong niya sapagkat alam naman natin na pag nabarahan dito 'yung tubig, maiipit at magko-cause ng flooding sa [North Luzon Expressway]. Hindi lang NLEX, kundi sa iba pang parte ng Metro Manila," MMDA General Manager Procopio Lipana, who oversaw the operation, said. | via ABSCBN News

ESTUDYANTE, NAHULOG SA ISANG CREEK SA PASONG TAMO, QUEZON CITY 
Isang babae na estudyante ang tinangay ng rumaragasang baha sa isang creek sa Brgy. Pasong Tamo, #QuezonCity nitong Huwebes, October 9.
Ayon sa mga saksi, nahulog ang estudyante sa isang ginagawang flood control project at tsaka tinangay ng malakas na agos ng tubig sa creek.
Nasagip naman ito ng mga residente na nag-abang sa isang tulay.

Matapos ang magnitude 7.6 na lindol na yumanig sa Davao Oriental ngayong araw, Oktubre 10, 2025, ilang gusali at establisimyento ang naiulat na gumuho at nagtamo ng pinsala.
Sa mga larawan na kuha matapos ang lindol, makikitang nagkabitak-bitak ang mga kalsada, may mga bumagsak na pader, at ilang bahay ang tuluyang nagiba dahil sa tindi ng pagyanig.
Patuloy na nagsasagawa ng rescue operations ang mga responders at LGUs sa apektadong lugar.
Pinapaalalahanan ang publiko na maging alerto sa mga aftershocks at manatili sa mga ligtas na lugar.
 Dasal para sa kaligtasan ng ating mga kababayan sa Davao Oriental at kalapit na probinsya.

NILIPAD 'YUNG MGA LOBO 
Uploader Filipina Maloto shared a video showing a bunch of balloons for sale accidentally floating away.
She looked for “Nanay,” the vendor often seen in front of the church in Concepcion, Marikina, bought some of her remaining balloons, and paid P1,000 to help out.
Nanay explained that she accidentally let go of the balloons while assisting a customer. “Bayaran pa naman ng bahay. Maiyak-iyak na ko talaga, pero nilalakasan ko lang ‘yung loob ko,” she said.
“Ang sabi ko po, sa kaniya na ‘yung sukli. Tapos ayun, sobrang saya ni Nanay napaiyak na kami parehas kasi ‘di siya makapaniwala,” the uploader recalled.
Meanwhile, the story touched many, inspiring donations of cash and groceries for Nanay.

“Ang Di‐Inaasahang Lindol sa Mindanao Kaninang Umaga”
Kanina lang umaga, isang malakas na lindol na may tinatayang magnitude 7.4 (o mas mataas pa sa ilang pagtataya) ang yumanig sa rehiyon ng Mindanao, lalong-lalo na sa baybayin ng Davao Oriental malapit sa bayan ng Manay. 
 Nagdulot ito ng pagyanig sa lupa sa maraming lugar, pagbagsak o pagbitak ng mga pader at gusali, pagkasira sa ospital, at pagka‐evacuate sa mga pasyente. 
 Mga coastal areas ay nilisan pansamantala dahil sa banta ng tsunami, bagaman kalaunan ay binawi ang tsunami alert. 
The Guardian
 Sa ngayon, kumpirmado nang may dalawang patay sa Davao Oriental dahil sa pagbagsak ng gusali. 
 Mysterious / Teoretikal na Pagsusuri
Pag‐galaw sa Philippine Trench
May teorya na ang lindol ay nagmula sa paggalaw ng isang segment sa Philippine Trench, isang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang mga tectonic plates sa ilalim ng dagat. 
 Ang ganitong pag‐galaw ay maaaring magtulak ng seabed pataas o pababa—na siya namang puwedeng magpagalaw ng tubig sa ibabaw, na nagiging sanhi ng tsunami. 
Submarine Landslides
Isang posibilidad ay may pagguho sa ilalim ng dagat (submarine landslide) na nangyari dahil sa malakas na get-o galaw ng lupa sa ilalim ng dagat. Ang ganitong pagguho ay puwedeng maglatag ng dagdag na gibain sa pagtaas o pagbaba ng tubig sa baybayin. Ito’y mas subtle at mahirap mapansin agad.
Aftershocks / Chain Reaction
Dahil dati’y nagkaroon ng malalakas na lindol sa iba’t ibang bahagi ng Pilipinas nitong mga nakaraang araw (halimbawa sa Cebu) 
, may posibilidad na ang stress sa mga fault lines ay nag‐accumulate. Kapag may lindol sa isang bahagi, maaaring magkaroon ito ng domino effect sa katabing faults.
Fault Complexity / Hidden Faults
Posible ring may hindi pa natutuklasang pinagsisikipan o fault line sa ilalim ng dagat o sa karatig na lupain. Sa ilang malalakas na lindol sa kasaysayan, lumitaw na may bahagi ng fault na hindi pa nakikita o hindi pa nailalarawan ng mga geologists.
Anomalous Phenomena / Sigaw ng Kalikasan
Sa aspetong “misteryoso,” may mga naniniwala rin sa mga sinaunang paniniwala—na ang lindol ay senyales mula sa kalikasan, o reaksyon sa masyadong labis na pagsamantala sa lupa, deforestation, pagmimina, o pagbabago sa ilalim ng dagat. Hindi ito sang‐ayon sa agham, ngunit madalas lumalabas sa mga lokal na kuwento at teoryang popular paminsan-minsan.
 Disclaimer (Para sa Edukasyunal na Layunin Lamang)
Ang nilalaman dito ay teoretikal at circumstantial lamang—hindi ito opisyal na ulat mula sa Phivolcs o iba pang mapagkakatiwalaang ahensya. Huwag ituring ito bilang huling hatol o totoong paliwanag. Para sa mas tamang impormasyon, mangyaring sumangguni sa Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) o lokal na awtoridad sa agham at kalikasang sakuna.

by: “manong do it”

Hindi ng langit, hindi ng kalikasan.
Basura sa kanal, siksik sa daan,

Kaya’t huwag tayong magtaka,
Kung taon-taon tayo’y lumulubog sa baha.
Sapagkat ang kalaban, hindi ulan —
Kundi ang ating sariling kapabayaan.

Senate President Pro Tempore Panfilo Lacson bared Thursday that there was a P355 million insertion in the 2025 national budget intended for Bulacan, which appears to match the claim of a DPWH engineer that Sen. Jinggoy Estrada allocated such amount in the spending plan.
Earlier this week, former DPWH Assistant District Engineer Brice Hernandez accused Estrada and Sen. Joel Villanueva of receiving "commitments" equal to about 30 percent of the project cost for some floodgates and pumping stations in Bulacan. 
"Si Senator Jinggoy po ay nagbaba ng P350 million ngayong 2025 sa ilang projects sa Bulacan... Ang kanyang SOP dito ay 30 percent, as per our district engineer Henry Alcantara. Diniliver ito noong lumabas ang mga item na ito sa GAA (General Appropriations Act)," Hernandez had said. | via ABS-CBN News

Nagmistulang ilog ang Malinis Road, Lemery matapos ang malakas na buhos ng ulan. Dahil dito, bumagal ang daloy ng trapiko at hirap ang mga motorista sa pagtawid sa baha. 
Ayon sa Batangas PIO, patuloy na inaasahan ang posibleng pagbaha sa ilang bayan ng lalawigan kaya’t pinapayuhan ang publiko na mag-ingat at umiwas muna sa pagbibiyahe sa binahang kalsada.
Sa listahan ng PAGASA sa “Flood Information”, ang Lemery ay nasa mga lugar na may Yellow Warning Level para sa pagbaha.

PAGASA: ASAHAN ANG MALAKAS NA ULAN MULA OKTUBRE HANGGANG PEBRERO DAHIL SA LA NIÑA 
Nagbabala ang PAGASA na posibleng maranasan ng bansa ang mas mataas sa normal na dami ng ulan mula Oktubre 2025 hanggang Pebrero 2026, lalo na sa silangang bahagi ng Pilipinas, dahil sa La Niña na kasalukuyang nararanasan sa tropical Pacific.
Ayon sa PAGASA, mas tataas pa ang tsansa ng malalakas na ulan at bagyo sa loob ng Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR). Maaari rin itong magdulot ng baha, flashfloods, at landslide sa mga bulubunduking lugar.
Ipinaliwanag ng ahensya na nagsimula pa noong Agosto 2025 ang paglamig ng temperatura sa karagatan, at umabot na ito sa La Niña threshold na -0.5°C nitong Setyembre.
“Asahan na magpapatuloy ang La Niña hanggang Disyembre–Enero–Pebrero 2025–2026 season, ayon sa mga climate models,” ayon sa PAGASA.

WATCH: The Discaya couple are saying goodbye to their chances of becoming state witness after deciding not to cooperate with the ICI investigation on the flood control scandal.
Ex-Supreme Court magistrate Antonio Carpio said the Discayas’ decision means they lose two benefits of being a state witness: freedom from criminal liability and forfeiture of assets.
“That will legitimize your stolen loot, the stolen money. That's why sabi ni dating DOJ secretary [Jesus Crispin Remulla], dapat magsauli siya. Anybody who wants to be in the state witness protection program must surrender what they stole.
Then we will give them the benefit of a state witness. Mukhang ayaw naman mag-surrender sila Discaya,” Carpio said in a DZMM interview.
Carpio said it was imperative for the justice chief to recover billions of pesos in estimated flood control kickbacks “dahil malilintikan siya, magagalit ang tao.”
The Discayas will also lose their protected status, which is temporary pending the evaluation of their application to become state witness. A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. Senator Bam Aquino's Philippine National Budget Blockchain Bill captured public attention, especially given the timing around flood-control controversies. The current outrage has ignited an important conversation on how public funds are spent-- and potentially hidden. In the uproar over stalled projects and missing allocations, the bill promised a clean fix: put every peso on the blockchain. Each transaction, it claimed, would live forever on an immutable ledger—visible to all, tamper-proof, and honest by design. It’s a seductive vision: that technology could finally do what politics hasn’t.
But that’s the problem. We keep mistaking technology for reform. Blockchain is treated as the cure, not the tool. As if corruption were a software bug, not a symptom of power, discretion, and inequality. The assumption is that when code is incorruptible, people will become so too. Yet history reminds us that tools inherit their makers’ hands—and their habits.

24-HOUR LOCALIZED WEATHER FORECAST FOR DAVAO REGION
Issued at    4:30 PM October 17, 2025
Valid Until 4:30 PM TOMORROW
SYNOPSIS: 
At 3:00 PM today, the center of Tropical Depression "RAMIL" was estimated based on all available data at 650 km East of Juban, Sorsogon (12.9°N, 130.0°E), with maximum sustained winds of 55 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 70 km/h. It is moving West Southwestward at 25 km/h. Localized Thunderstorms affecting DAVAO REGION. 
FORECAST:  
DAVAO REGION will have a partly clody to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to  Localized Thunderstorms . Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from Northwest to Southwest with slight to moderate seas.
 ( Wave Height 0.6 to 1.5 meters).
KAUGALINGONG PINULUNGAN: 
Ang dakbayan sa Dabaw ug ubang dapit sa REHIYON SA DABAW makasinati  sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan nga adunay mga pagdag-um inubanan sa katag-katag nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta sa panahon nga adunay severe thunderstorms o grabe na bundak sa ulan. Hinay ngadto na sa kasarangan nga hangin gikan sa Amihanang-kasadpan ngadto sa Habatang-kasadpan nga direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto  sa kasarangan ang pagbalud. Tropical Cyclone Update #RamilPH
5AM, October 18, 2025
Ramil intensifies into a tropical storm.
Wind signal no. 2 is now up over Camarines Norte, Catanduanes, and northern Camarines Sur.
At 4 a.m. Saturday, tropical storm Ramil was located 305 km east of Juban, Sorsogon. It now packs winds of 65 kph and gusts up to 80 kph. It is moving westward at 20 kph.
Ramil may make landfall or pass close over Catanduanes this afternoon or evening.
It will then pass close to Camarines Norte and Polillo Islands Sunday morning before making another landfall over Aurora or Isabela later in the morning or afternoon.
A northward or southward shift in the track could result to different landfall areas.
Ramil will cross Northern Luzon and emerge over the West Philippine Sea in the afternoon or evening.
It may exit the Philippine area of responsibility on Monday morning.
Ramil will bring significant rains over parts of Eastern Visayas and most of Luzon through Monday.
Heavy to intense rainfall is expected over Samar Island, Catanduanes, and Sorsogon this Saturday and over northern Bicol, Quezon, Aurora, and Isabela on Sunday.
Widespread and serious flooding and landslides are likely in many areas.
Up to two meter storm surge may also be generated along the coasts of Samar Island, Bicol Region, Quezon, Marinduque, Central Luzon, Isabela, and Ilocos Region.

The Independent Commission for Infrastructure is eyeing to “seize and freeze” assets of flood control players to speed up the recovery of billions of pesos in government funds allegedly lost to the scam.
ICI Executive Director Brian Hosaka said that aside from the filing of criminal charges, the ICI is also focusing on asset recovery with the help of 15-17 government agencies.
He said the Anti-Money Laundering Council, Office of the Solicitor General and the Ombudsman could seek to freeze accounts of persons linked to government irregularities while the Bureau of Customs could seize assets such as luxury cars of flood control players.
He also downplayed the decision of the Discaya couple not to cooperate with the ICI, saying the body can tap other witnesses and other sources of information.
"The fact that they are invoking [the right against self-incrimination]... is reason for us to investigate harder," Hosaka said.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla earlier chided the couple for refusing to tell all in the ICI inquiry, adding that the two seem to be protecting a lot of people.
He added blanket immunity is impossible for the Discayas since they are accused of too many crimes including bribery and tax evasion. BAGYONG ‘RAMIL’, LUMAKAS PA HABANG PAPALAPIT SA BICOL REGION 
Lumakas pa bilang Tropical Storm ang bagyong #RamilPH na may int’l name na ngayong #FENGSHEN habang patuloy na tinutumbok ang probinsya ng #Catanduanes sa #BicolRegion.
Taglay ngayon ng bagyo ang lakas ng hangin na umaabot sa 65 kph at pagbugsong umaabot sa 80 kph. Kumikilos ito sa direksyong West Northwestward sa bilis na 15 kph.
Mamayang hapon inaasahang tuluyan na itong magla-landfall sa probinsya ng #Catanduanes at inaasahang didikit sa kabikulan bago tuluyang mag-landfall muli sa bahagi ng #Quezon-#Aurora area bukas ng umaga at maghapong tatawirin ang kalupaan ng #Northern-#CentralLuzon area.
Asahan na ang masamang panahon sa malaking bahagi ng #Visayas at sa #BicolRegion ngayong araw dahil sa direktang epekto ng bagyo habang  asahan na rin ang mga pag-ulan sa #CALABARZON, #MetroManila, #CentralLuzon, at sa #CagayanValley dahil sa trough ng bagyo.
Bukas mas mararamdaman ang masungit na lagay ng panahon sa malaking bahagi ng #Luzon dahil sa inaasahang pagtawid ng bagyo sa kalupaan.
Patuloy na pinag-iingat ang ating mga kababayan na maaapektuhan ng bagyo sa banta ng mga biglaang pagbaha at mga pagguho ng lupa na kaakibat ng mga pag-ulan na dala ng bagyo.
Manatiling mag-monitor ng mga susunod pang update hinggil dito.

“Halata naman na pinipilit niyong ilihis ang totoong problema — ang flood control at korapsyon n’yo sa Kongreso. Baka gusto mong ayusin muna ’yang problema na ’yan sa lugar mo bago ka maghanap ng gulo sa labas ng sariling bakuran mo,” Duterte said.
He added that Ortega should focus on addressing problems in his district — or “try podcasting” if he’s more interested in making noise than in legislating.

TROPICAL STORM RAMIL MAKES LANDFALL IN SORSOGON; HEAVY RAINS THREATEN LUZON AND VISAYAS
Tropical Storm Ramil (international name: Fengshen) has officially made landfall in southeastern Luzon, near Sorsogon and the Bicol Region, after tracking slightly farther south and west than early forecasts predicted.
Now moving slowly westward, Ramil is expected to cross the Bicol Region before heading toward Southern and Central Luzon, including areas near Metro Manila and Pangasinan, throughout the weekend.
PAGASA has raised Signal No. 2 over parts of Northern Samar and the eastern coast. However, the main concern is heavy rainfall, not wind — with 100 to 200 mm expected along the east coast and 50 to 150 mm across Bicol, Samar, and eventually much of Luzon.
Residents are warned of localized flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous and low-lying areas. Even regions north of the storm’s center may experience widespread rain due to its broad convection.
Authorities urge the public to stay alert and not focus solely on the storm’s center track, as outer rainbands often cause the most significant impacts.

text: IN PHOTOS Sa kabila ng maulang panahon, naglunsad ng kilos-protesta sa Freedom Park ang iba't-ibang progresibong sektor at ang mga taong-simbahan upang tutulan ang lumalalang krisis sa lipunan at bilang paggunita sa Buwan ng mga Pesante, Oktubre 21.  Kasabay nito, bitbit nila ang ilan sa mga panawagan sa gitna ng sala-salabat na isyu: agarang aksyon para sa tunay na reporma sa lupa, hustisya para sa mga biktima ng mga human rights violations sa rehiyon, at pagpapanagot sa lahat ng mga sangkot sa korapsyon at laban sa malawakang katiwalian. text: WAIST-DEEP FLOODWATERS IN KAWIT, CAVITE Residents were forced to wade through chest-deep floodwaters along Toclong-San Sebastian Road and Tramo Street in Barangay Gahak, Kawit, Cavite after a nearby river overflowed amid continuous monsoon rains on August 8, 2026. text: LOOK:|BEHIND EVERY NUMBER: THE HUMAN HEARTBREAK OF NEPAL’S FLASH FLOOD. August 29, 2026 — One can scarcely imagine the terror: standing inside your own home, hearing the roar of water, mud, and rocks approaching — and having only seconds to wonder if your family will survive. That was the reality for communities along the Nepal–Tibet border on August 26, 2026, when a massive glacier and rock collapse triggered a catastrophic flash flood along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers. Homes, roads, bridges, power plants, and entire settlements were swept away — often with little or no warning.  IN THOSE FINAL MOMENTS Residents were forced to scramble to rooftops, balconies, or any higher ground available — clinging to hope as waters rose nearly 30 feet in half an hour. We may never fully know what went through their minds: Were they crying? Calling loved ones? Praying? Holding each other? What we do know is that behind every statistic is a human life, a family, and a story of heartbreak.  THE SCALE OF LOSS - 469 confirmed dead — and still rising - Hundreds more remain missing, including tourists and pilgrims from several nations - Entire communities buried under mud and debris - Rescue teams continue to reach isolated areas "Behind every number is a family waiting. Behind every missing person is someone desperately hoping. And behind every survivor is a story of courage."  May rescuers reach those still waiting. May the missing be found. And may every grieving family find strength in this time of unimaginable loss.  ,///Charlie. #PrayForNepal #NepalFlood #HimalayanDisaster #FlashFlood #DisasterAwareness #HopeAndPrayer #BosesNgPilipinas See less LOOK:|BEHIND EVERY NUMBER: THE HUMAN HEARTBREAK OF NEPAL’S FLASH FLOOD.

text: DAVAO: THE “FLOOD CAPITAL” — BUT PERHAPS NOT FOR THE REASON YOU THINK They say Davao is the “Flood Capital of the Philippines.” Well, if someone insists on giving us that crown, perhaps we should wear it proudly—but let’s first ask a simple question: What exactly is overflowing?  Yes, Davao experiences floods. We have rivers that swell after relentless rain, low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature, sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment, and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools. That is a real problem. It deserves real solutions—not political theater. But if we are going to compare cities, perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan. During the severe southwest monsoon flooding in July 2025, for example, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across Metro Manila within a single day. So before anyone points a finger at Davao, perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city. Water does not check political affiliations before it rises. Rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours. And rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches.  But here's where I see Davao differently. Because there is another kind of flooding happening here—one that doesn't destroy homes, close roads, or leave mud behind. Davao floods with culture. Walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of Mindanao: Indigenous traditions, migrant communities, different languages, cuisines, beliefs, stories, and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry. Ask someone where they came from, and you may discover an entire story behind the answer. Then, inevitably, there's food. Because in Davao, you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian.  “This variety is sweeter.” “No, that one has better texture.” “You haven't tried the best one yet.” Suddenly, what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian. No registration fee required.  But perhaps Davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture. It is warmth. There is a quiet generosity in the character of many Dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure. You can arrive as a stranger and, before long, someone may already be telling you where to eat, what places to visit, which shortcut to take—and, most importantly, which road to avoid when traffic is terrible. That's not just hospitality. That's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory.  And then there is Davao's natural beauty. The sea. Samal. Mount Apo. The forests. The farms. The rivers. The mountains. The wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies. Davao is also changing. Businesses are arriving. Buildings are rising. Infrastructure is expanding. Communities are growing. People continue to come—not only because they are looking for jobs, but because they are looking for possibilities. Some arrive carrying résumés. Others arrive carrying business plans. Some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream. And somewhere along the way, many discover something unexpected: They don't merely live in Davao. They become part of it. That, perhaps, is the real story. A city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it. text: 10/9 7AM Update: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a major Category 3 hurricane with max sustained winds of 120 mph. The storm will begin weakening prior to landfall along our coast this evening, but it will still be a SIGNIFICANT hurricane upon impact.  All last minute preparations should be rushed to completion this morning. Residents and tourists should follow the advice given by local officials and evacuate immediately if told to do so.  Here are the latest details:  Timing & Track: Deteriorating conditions through the day today with rain spreading north and tropical storm force winds starting as early as noon. The worst conditions are expected from late afternoon through late evening as the center makes landfall, likely between Mobile Bay and Choctawhatchee Bay.  Storm Surge: Potential for 6-9 feet for the western Florida Panhandle, 4-6 ft for the Alabama coastline, and 3-5 ft for Mobile Bay. Surge will be highest near and east of the track, while areas west of the track may experience low water levels around landfall.  Winds: Upon approach, widespread tropical storm force winds and wind damage will occur well away from the center, with damaging hurricane-force winds near the center close to the coast. Expect winds to cause structural damage and knock down trees/powerlines, leading numerous power outages.  Flooding: Heavy rain near the core of the storm and in bands well east of the center could cause significant flash flooding, especially on saturated ground and in urban areas. text: PUMP BOY NAKURYENTEHAN, NALUMOS SA BAHA SA BUHANGIN  A 21-year-old pump boy was found lifeless after reportedly being electrocuted and drowning in floodwaters in New San Isidro, Barangay Buhangin, Davao City at around 2:35 AM on May 19, 2026. The victim, a single man from Manay, Davao Oriental, was reportedly renting a place in the area when the incident occurred. Police from Station 5 – Buhangin, together with barangay responders and Central 911 rescue teams, were conducting flood monitoring and rescue operations when they discovered the victim floating in front of his boarding house around 2:00 AM. He was immediately brought to the Southern Philippines Medical Center (SPMC), but was later declared dead by attending physicians. His cause of death was listed as cardiopulmonary arrest secondary to fatal cardiac dysrhythmia due to electrocution, with acute respiratory failure secondary to drowning. The victim’s remains are currently at the hospital morgue and may undergo autopsy. via  Superbalita Davao  DCPO  #AllYouNeedToKnow See less PUMP BOY NAKURYENTEHAN, NALUMOS SA BAHA SA BUHANGIN

text: Honestly, the flooding discourse these past few days showed how people online would rather push hate and politics than actually understand what happened  Since May 17 pa unstable na ang weather sa Davao. Then May 18 to May 19 halos tuloy tuloy na ang moderate to heavy rain with thunderstorms and flood advisories especially sa low-lying areas. As in HOURS yung ulan, hindi yung typical na “saglit lang naman umulan.” Pero pagdating online, parang nawalan lahat ng common sense  Suddenly: “Davao can never.” “Singapore nga hindi binabaha.” “51 billion flood control nasan na?” “DDS delusion.” “Supercity pero bahain.” Like damn, everybody became engineers, meteorologists, and urban planners overnight  Nobody is saying “okay lang ang baha.” Of course frustrating siya. Residents were affected. Motorists and commuters got stranded. Valid lahat ng reklamo about needing better drainage, better urban planning, and better maintenance. Pero ang weird kasi some people are acting like: 1. walang nonstop heavy rain for almost 2 to 3 days 2. walang low-lying flood-prone areas 3. walang factor ang geography ng Davao at parang unique sa Davao ang flooding during extreme weather People also keep screaming about the “₱51 billion flood control” without even reading the actual reports   Even clarified na hindi yan purely flood control. Kasama diyan roads, bridges, bypass roads, coastal roads, drainage works, river defense projects, and other infrastructure allocations from 2020–2022. Hindi yan parang: insert ₱51B charaaaan flood immunity unlocked! And about geography, people forget na Davao catches runoff from the Mt. Apo system and even southeastern Bukidnon. Water naturally flows down toward the city and low-lying coastal areas especially during prolonged rainfall. Hindi mo yan ma-o-off like a faucet habang tuloy tuloy ang buhos ng ulan  Even countries like Japan, Singapore, and the Netherlands, places people love comparing Davao to, STILL experience flooding during extreme rainfall despite decades of engineering and trillions invested in flood mitigation. Flood control reduces risk. It doesn’t magically delete water from existence. Criticism is valid. Demanding accountability is valid. Pero yung obvious hatebait, fake engineering takes, fearbaiting, at pag-ignore sa actual weather conditions just to push a political narrative? That’s where people start rolling their eyes  #DavaoFlood #DavaoCity #FloodControl #DutertePaRin See less Honestly, the flooding discourse these past few days showed how people online would rather push hate and politics than actually understand what happened

text: "OO, RESIDENTE AKO NG DAVAO CITY"  Kinuwestiyon ni dating Philippine National Police (PNP) Chief Nicolas Torre III ang patuloy na pagbaha sa Davao City matapos muling bahain ang kanyang bahay sa NHA Bangkal, Barangay Talomo kasunod ng malakas na ulan noong Hulyo 24. Sa kanyang social media post, sinabi ni Torre na nakapangalan sa kanya at sa kanyang asawa ang naturang bahay at bilang residente ng Davao City ay may karapatan siyang magtanong kung bakit paulit-ulit pa ring nangyayari ang pagbaha. Ayon kay Torre, matagal nang alam na ang mga sanhi ng pagbaha tulad ng mountain runoff at malalakas na pag-ulan, kaya dapat aniya ay may epektibong solusyon na, lalo na't bilyon-bilyong piso na ang nagastos para sa mga flood control projects. Binigyang-diin niya na ang tunay na sukatan ng flood control ay hindi ang dami ng proyektong naipatupad kundi ang dami ng pamilyang hindi na naaabot ng baha. "Naghahanap ako ng resulta, hindi ng palusot," saad ni Torre. #LNB See less "OO, RESIDENTE AKO NG DAVAO CITY"

text: Warning Signs: Two Major Drug Busts Show The Philippines Is Being Targeted Two massive drug seizures in neighboring countries are sounding a clear alarm: the Philippines is being directly targeted by major drug syndicates, and we cannot afford to ignore the risk.  Bust #1: 521 KG of Meth Seized From Private Jet in Laos October 1, 2026 At Luang Prabang International Airport, Laotian authorities intercepted a private jet carrying a staggering 521 kilograms of methamphetamine — packed into 21 suitcases. Malaysia’s Narcotics Crime Investigation Department confirmed the drugs came from Laos and were bound for Manila, Philippines. Thirteen people were arrested — including a Singaporean pilot, a Malaysian co-pilot, a Filipino passenger, and Laotian nationals. This wasn’t a small-time operation; it was a sophisticated, international delivery flying straight to our shores.  Bust #2: Over 1 Tonne of Ice Seized in Gulf of Thailand, Headed for PH October 8, 2026 Thai Marine Police and the Narcotics Suppression Division intercepted a vessel in the lower Gulf of Thailand after careful surveillance. Hidden in a secret compartment at the stern, they found 1,178 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine ("ice") — packed into 39 sacks. Police confirmed the vessel was actively preparing to transport the shipment to the Philippines. That’s over 1.1 tonnes of dangerous drugs — enough to flood communities and destroy countless lives.  The Bigger Picture These aren’t isolated incidents. In just one week, nearly 1.7 tonnes of meth bound for the Philippines was intercepted outside our borders. It shows our country is being targeted by large-scale, well-organized drug networks. This is exactly why we must take the risk of narco-state tendencies seriously. When powerful syndicates treat our nation as a primary destination for their shipments, it threatens our communities, our youth, and our institutions. The drugs may have been seized abroad — but the warning is for us. We need stronger border intelligence, better regional coordination, and greater vigilance at home. Let’s not wait until these shipments start arriving successfully. Our safety depends on staying one step ahead.  #NarcoState See less Warning Signs: Two Major Drug Busts Show The Philippines Is Being Targeted

text: HURRICANE ISAIAS STRENGTHENS TO 110 MPH — MAJOR HURRICANE STATUS POSSIBLE THIS MORNING!  NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER: RUSH ALL PREPARATIONS TO COMPLETION — WEATHER CONDITIONS WILL DETERIORATE RAPIDLY TODAY!  Friday, October 9, 2026  4:00 AM CDT — NHC Advisory Number 11  Mississippi • Alabama • Florida Panhandle • Southeastern Louisiana Accuracy Over First — Facts, Not Fear  DANGEROUS HURRICANE ISAIAS CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN AS IT APPROACHES THE NORTHERN GULF COAST! Hurricane Isaias has strengthened to 110 mph, placing it just below Category 3 intensity on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. According to the National Hurricane Center’s 4:00 AM advisory, Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that Isaias continues to intensify, and the hurricane is likely to reach major hurricane strength this morning. Although some weakening is forecast before landfall, Isaias is expected to remain a dangerous hurricane capable of producing destructive winds, life-threatening storm surge, flooding rainfall and tornadoes.  The time for hurricane preparations is rapidly running out across portions of the northern Gulf Coast. ⸻  LATEST HURRICANE INFORMATION — 4:00 AM CDT *   Maximum sustained winds: 110 mph, with higher gusts. *   Minimum central pressure: 963 millibars. *   Location: 26.4°N, 88.0°W. *   Movement: North-northeast at 15 mph. *   Distance: Approximately 200 miles south-southeast of the mouth of the Mississippi River. *   Hurricane-force winds: Extend outward up to 30 miles from the center. *   Tropical-storm-force winds: Extend outward up to 185 miles from the center. *   Aircraft reconnaissance: Air Force and NOAA Hurricane Hunters confirm strengthening.  FORECAST TRACK AND LANDFALL The National Hurricane Center expects Isaias to turn more toward the north later today. *   Friday afternoon: Hurricane Isaias approaches the northern Gulf Coast. *   Friday afternoon and evening: Tropical-storm-force winds spread across portions of the warning areas. *   Friday night into early Saturday: Landfall is expected somewhere within the Hurricane Warning area. *   Intensity: Isaias could become a Category 3 hurricane this morning before undergoing some weakening ahead of landfall. IMPORTANT: The exact location of landfall remains uncertain. Dangerous conditions will extend well away from the center, especially east of the track. ⸻  HURRICANE AND TROPICAL STORM WARNINGS  HURRICANE WARNING From Ocean Springs, Mississippi, eastward to the Bay/Gulf County line in Florida. Hurricane conditions are expected somewhere within this warning area tonight into early Saturday.  TROPICAL STORM WARNING * Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line, Louisiana, to west of Ocean Springs, Mississippi. * East of the Bay/Gulf County line, Florida, to the Aucilla River. Tropical-storm-force winds are expected to begin affecting portions of these areas today.  STORM SURGE WARNING From the mouth of the Mississippi River eastward to the Suwannee River, Florida. A Storm Surge Watch remains in effect from the Suwannee River to Yankeetown, Florida. ⸻  LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE — UP TO 7 FEET POSSIBLE! The National Hurricane Center forecasts dangerous storm surge flooding along portions of the northern Gulf Coast. Forecast peak water levels above normally dry ground: *   Dauphin Island, AL, to Indian Pass, FL: 5–7 feet. *   Indian Pass to Steinhatchee River, FL: 4–6 feet. *   Mouth of Mississippi River to Dauphin Island: 3–5 feet. *   Mobile Bay: 3–5 feet. *   Steinhatchee River to Suwannee River: 3–5 feet. *   Suwannee River to Yankeetown: 2–4 feet. *   Lake Pontchartrain: 1–3 feet.  These values represent potential inundation above ground level, not wave heights. Large, dangerous waves may accompany the surge. Residents in evacuation zones should follow instructions from local emergency management officials immediately. ⸻  HEAVY RAINFALL — 4 TO 8 INCHES, LOCALLY 15 INCHES! Significant flooding is expected across portions of the Southeast through the weekend. Greatest rainfall threat: *   Southern Alabama. *   Florida Panhandle and Big Bend. *   Southwestern Georgia. Expected rainfall: 4–8 inches, with localized totals up to 15 inches, especially where rainbands repeatedly move across the same communities. Across other portions of the Southeast, 2–5 inches are forecast, with isolated totals approaching 10 inches.  Flash flooding, urban flooding and significant river flooding are possible. Never drive across flooded roads. Turn Around, Don’t Drown! ⸻  TORNADO THREAT INCREASES LATE TODAY As Isaias approaches the coast, rotating thunderstorms within the hurricane’s outer rainbands could produce tornadoes. Friday afternoon and tonight: * Coastal Alabama. * Florida Panhandle. * Far southwestern Georgia. Saturday: * Eastern Alabama. * Florida Panhandle. * Georgia. * Portions of the Carolinas. Tornadoes associated with landfalling tropical cyclones can develop quickly and sometimes provide very little warning. Keep multiple ways to receive weather alerts. ⸻  MISSISS

text: via  Dost_pagasa  SEVERE WEATHER BULLETIN #5 FOR TROPICAL STORM "#AuringPH" (DUJUAN) SIGNAL NO. 1 Davao Oriental Davao de Oro Agusan del Sur Surigao del Sur TROPICAL CYCLONE: WARNING ISSUED AT 5:00 AM, 19 February 2021 (Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin to be issued at 11 AM today) TROPICAL STORM "AURING" HAS REMAINED ALMOST STATIONARY OVER THE PHILIPPINE SEA EAST OF MINDANAO. Hazards affecting land areas: Heavy Rainfall:  • Today through tomorrow early morning, light to moderate with at times heavy rainshowers over Caraga, Davao Oriental, Davao de Oro, and Davao del Norte. • Tomorrow early morning through Sunday early morning, moderate to heavy with at times intense rains over Caraga Region, Davao Oriental, and Davao de Oro. Moderate to heavy rains over Eastern Visayas, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Bukidnon, and Davao del Norte. Light to moderate with at times heavy rains over the rest of Visayas, the rest of Northern Mindanao, Albay, Sorsogon, Catanduanes, Masbate, Lanao del Sur, Cotabato, and Davao City. • Under these conditions, scattered to widespread flooding (including flashfloods) and rain-induced landslides are likely during heavy rains or prolonged rainfall especially in areas that are highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards as identified in hazard maps. Adjacent or nearby areas may also experience flooding in the absence of such rainfall occurrence due to surface runoff or swelling of river channels. PAGASA Regional Services Divisions may issue local thunderstorm/rainfall advisories and heavy rainfall warnings while the Hydrometeorology Division and River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning Centers may issue General Flood Advisories and Basin Flood Bulletins as appropriate. Strong Winds:  • The surge of the Northeast Monsoon is already bringing strong breeze to near-gale conditions with occasionally higher gusts over Northern Luzon and the eastern sections of Central Luzon, Southern Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. especially in coastal and mountainous areas. The affected localities include those currently under Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal #1. However, strong breeze to near-gale conditions directly associated with “AURING” will likely begin to prevail over the wind signal areas on Saturday at the earliest. • More localities in Caraga and Davao Region may be placed under TCWS #1 in the next bulletin. Based on current meteorological data, the highest level of wind signal that will be issued throughout the passage of “AURING” is TCWS #2 (for potentially damaging gale-force to storm-force winds). Hazards affecting coastal waters: • In the next 24 hours, rough to high seas (3.0 to 6.5 m) will be experienced over the eastern seaboard of Mindanao. Rough to very rough seas are also expected over the seaboards of Northern Luzon and the eastern seaboards of Central Luzon (3.0 to 5.5 m), Southern Luzon (4.0 to 5.5 m), and Visayas (3.5 to 6.0 m). Sea travel is risky for all types of sea vessels over these waters. • Moderate to rough seas (1.2 to 3.0 m) will be experienced over the rest of the seaboards of the country. Mariners of small seacrafts are advised to take precautionary measures when venturing out to sea. Inexperienced mariners should avoid navigating in these conditions.  Track and intensity outlook: • Tropical Storm “AURING” will move generally westward or west-southwestward slowly over the next 24 hours before turning northwestward tomorrow morning while accelerating. “AURING” is forecast to make landfall over the eastern coast of Caraga Region on Sunday (21 February). On the forecast track, the storm will likely follow a generally northwestward path as it traverses Caraga Region, Visayas, and MIMAROPA on Sunday and Monday. • “AURING” is forecast to further intensity into a Severe Tropical Storm in the next 48 hours. However, the storm will likely weaken while crossing the archipelago due to significant terrain interaction and dry air intrusion from the Northeast Monsoon. Location of eye/center: At 4:00 AM today, the center of Tropical Storm "AURING" was estimated based on all available data at 595 km East Southeast of Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur (7.2°N, 131.6°E).   Strength: Maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 90 km/h.  Movement: Almost Stationary   Forecast Positions  • 24 Hour (Tomorrow morning): 395 km East Southeast of Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur (7.1°N, 129.7°E) • 48 Hour (Sunday morning):230 km East Southeast of Surigao City, Surigao del Norte (9.2°N, 127.5°E) • 72 Hour (Monday morning): 60 km East of Roxas City, Capiz (11.5°N, 123.3°E) • 96 Hour (Tuesday morning):225 km West of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro (13.2°N, 119.1°E) • 120 Hour (Wednesday morning):330 km West of Subic Bay (14.3°N, 117.3°E)  TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNAL TCWS 1 (30-60 km/h winds prevailing or expected in 36 hours)  Davao Oriental, the eastern portion of Davao de Oro (Pantukan, Maragusan, New Bataan, Compostela, Monkayo), the southeastern portion of Agusan del Sur

text: A SEA OF TRASH FLOODS THE RIVER BESIDE BACLARAN CHURCH A massive accumulation of garbage from Manila Bay filled the river in front of Baclaran Church in Parañaque City on Monday, August 10, as heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or Habagat swept debris into the area. The thick layer of floating waste created an alarming scene, with trash covering a large portion of the waterway. Nearby residents said they had never experienced anything like this before, highlighting the unusual scale of the debris buildup following the heavy rainfall. The incident once again raises concerns about waste management, waterways, and the impact of heavy rains on communities near Manila Bay. text: ₱47-M Flood Control Project in Laoag Collapses — Ties Emerge Between  Contractor Linked to Davao Lawmaker and Sandro Marcos’ Office A newly built flood control structure along Padsan River in Barangay Gabu, Laoag City — a project worth ₱47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 General Appropriations Act (GAA) — has collapsed JUST MONTHS after its reported completion, sparking fresh outrage over the alleged “flood-control mafia” operating in Congress. Photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked, dislodged, and washed into the river, exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion.  The project billboard names RA Pahati Construction & Supply, Inc. as the contractor, under the DPWH Ilocos Norte First District Engineering Office, with a target completion date of October 4, 2024. RA Pahati Construction is reportedly owned by the family of Rep. Jhong Ceniza of Pantukan, Davao de Oro — a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles.  Sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that RA Pahati has become a favored builder for Rep. Sandro Marcos, the Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative, allegedly with some help from his chief of staff, said to be a relative of Rep. Ceniza’s wife. Residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse, noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks. Infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction, adequate riprap foundation, and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction — all of which appear deficient in the broken sections. The collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a “cash cow” for certain districts.  RA Pahati, controlled by the Ceniza family, has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across Luzon and Mindanao, despite originating from Davao de Oro. In Ilocos Norte, whispers persist that Rep. Sandro Marcos’ chief of staff — reportedly related by marriage to the Cenizas — has been instrumental in channeling projects to RA Pahati, bypassing stricter vetting.  Political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son, especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive DPWH flood control budgets. The incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide, long suspected to be overpriced, poorly built, and politically manipulated.  In Congress, several lawmakers — particularly from Mindanao — have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals. Observers warn that this Laoag project could become a flashpoint, especially since it sits in the home turf of the President’s son, who is expected to champion good governance but now faces scrutiny over his district’s infrastructure spending. text: While Quezon City is drowning, where is Vince? Cars are being swallowed by floodwaters. Major roads have turned into rivers. Residents are struggling to get through streets that should never have become impassable. And yet, one question keeps rising above the floodwater: #NasaanSiVince? It is about holding him accountable for the infrastructure his department is responsible for. Inspections are not enough. Press releases are not enough. Promises are not enough. When flood-control projects are supposed to protect communities, the public has every right to ask whether those projects are actually working. Because when the roads become rivers and cars become floating objects, something clearly isn't working. So, Secretary Vince Dizon, where are you? The public doesn't need another photo opportunity beside a flooded road. They need answers. They need action. And most of all, they need to know why—after billions have been poured into flood-control infrastructure—Filipinos are still drowning in the same streets. #NasaanSiVince See less While Quezon City is drowning, where is Vince?

text: When the Waters Rise in Davao City, So Do the Online Critics Following the heavy rains brought by the Habagat and recent weather systems on July 24, 2026, several neighborhoods across Davao City once again faced rising floodwaters. From Mandug and Tugbok down to low-lying areas like Bangkal, Matina, and Talomo, families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels, moving to higher ground, or waiting for emergency teams. And like clockwork, as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media, the comments section lit up with the usual outrage, political potshots, and online bashing. "Where did the billions go?" "Why hasn't the city solved flooding yet?" It is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes. But using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science, geography, and non-stop work happening on the ground. Here is the perspective every Dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear. 1. You Cannot Out-Engineer a Catch Basin No politician, regardless of their party, and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography. Davao City sits beside major river systems (Davao, Talomo, Matina, Lipadas, Bunawan, and Lasang) flowing straight into the gulf. Key areas like Bago Gallera, Talomo Proper, Ulas, Bangkal, and Matina are natural catch basins. When continuous rains hit the highlands upstream, millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations. Add a high tide at the coast, and the ocean acts like a giant dam, preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea. Dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow, but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean. 2. Nature Remembers Its Original Shape Parts of Boulevard, Bucana, Agdao, and Sta. Ana were historically mudflats, swamps, and coastal wetlands. Humans can pave over these landscapes with roads, subdivisions, and concrete structures, but when extreme rainfall happens, water simply reclaims its natural pathways. With climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide, rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year. This is a regional and global environmental challenge, not an isolated municipal flaw. 3. "Where Did the Funds Go?" Look at the Defense Systems in Place Critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear. But flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling; it's built to slow down water, protect riverbanks, and buy critical time.  Pumping Stations & Retarding Basins: Built in notorious bottlenecks (like Sasa and La Verna) to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers.  Revetment Walls & Dikes: Miles of concrete dikes line the Matina, Talomo, and Davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges.  Early Warning & River Monitoring: The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) operates automated sensors and live HD monitoring cameras along all six major river channels, allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks. 4. While Keyboard Warriors Bash, Responders Are Out in the Dark While critics type away in dry rooms, hundreds of frontline responders, from the CDRRMO, BFP, Davao Light, urban search and rescue (SAR) units, and barangay disaster teams, are out in waist-deep water, executing rescue operations, clearing clogged channels, and moving stranded families to safety. Good governance in a coastal, river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities; it’s measured by preparedness, quick response, and zero casualties. The fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system. Bashing Davao City during a flood won't lower the tide, and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain. Instead of tearing each other down, let’s focus on what actually keeps us safe: community preparedness and cooperation. When the CDRRMO issues a Code Red or sounds the warning siren, do not wait. Follow evacuation protocols early. Look out for elderly neighbors, keep your emergency kits ready, and respect the responders risking their safety on the frontlines.

text: METRO MANILA FACES SEVERE INUNDATION DESPITE PREVIOUS DISASTER FOCUS ON MINDANAO Netizens Contrast NCR Flood Crisis with Normal Daily Life in Davao City Following Palace Statements MANILA, Philippines — Heavy downpours have left vast portions of Metro Manila submerged, sparking renewed public discussion over recent statements by Presidential Communications Office Undersecretary Castro regarding regional flood vulnerabilities. Earlier comments from Usec. Castro highlighted Davao as a primary center for flooding concerns in the country. However, current conditions show the National Capital Region bearing the brunt of severe waterlogging, causing major traffic disruptions and stranded commuters across key thoroughfares. Meanwhile, viral footage and social media posts show residents in Davao City enjoying routine outdoor activities, including community basketball games, under manageable weather conditions. Local authorities in Metro Manila are currently deploying emergency teams and pumps to clear inundated avenues, while disaster management officials reiterate that flood monitoring remains active nationwide regardless of shifting weather patterns. text: DAVAO FLOODING IS NOT A CORRUPTION ISSUE 1. IT IS a calamity issue - Singapore, the US, Dubai, and other cities also had their fair share of flooding - For Davao, it rained heavily for at least 5 nights, thunderstorms, almost all night. But flooding did not happen until the 4th or 5th night.  This means, of course, the ground is loose, basins are filled, and calamities can occur. - Flooding happened in areas close to the river and low-lying areas, which is a small portion of the whole city. Only 358 families were reported to be affected.  - But for Davao, we had minimal effects. If this had happened elsewhere, it could have been worse. Our LGU learned from the 2011 incident. Our 51-B flood control project protected MILLIONS of us.  2. IT IS NOT a Preparedness-Issue - Unlike other cities, our LGU has a world-class disaster and risk management plan.  - Our 911 is world-class. - Our disaster and rescue facilities and equipment are world-class - Talk about our taxes-well spent - Talk about the years of good governance of the  City Government of Davao - Living in Davao, we feel safe even in calamities, knowing that our LGU will have early warning protocols, search and rescue operations directives, and the PEOPLE OF DAVAO who are there to help each other. - Yes, even if our LGU is there, Davaoeños are also there for the government and for each other. This is why Davao has eagle-like resilience. 3. IT IS NOT a Governance-Issue -  Davao has a working City Social Services and Development Office (CCSDO). It is an exclusive arm of the city to take care of us in case of any fire, flood, or other calamities. - They are seen and felt. They are usually first on the ground to give warm food, clothing, mental health assistance, etc., during disasters. - Baranggay and city officials are mostly on the ground before, during, and after a calamity to facilitate and assist their residents in getting back to its feet. One family at a time, one day at a time. - Suppliers like water,  power, (internet - not so sure), will do their best to restore services asap. OUR CITY OFFICIALS, the Dutertes, are not corrupt and poor in their governance.  This city can withstand trials because we were built to withstand any, YESTERDAY, not when disasters strike. Will calamities hit the city? Big YES! Will we be affected by it?  Also YES! Is our LGU perfect? NO. Is our LGU dependable in times of crisis? Big YES! The effect is not as bad. Because of the last few decades of being raised by the Dutertes, this city is positioned to be forward-thinking. We were able to build this city surge into any economic and natural disaster challenges. So stop bashing the city with its small hit as if it has fallen big time, because even if we were hit, good governance has protected many. This is not like your city, and our experience is not like yours, which shaped your current judgment. And NO, this is not a "zombie-type" and blind following a persona, a name, or a party. Davaoeños are better than that. We will hold our leaders accountable if they mess up.  So stop using a calamity-based hit to shape a political narrative that doesn't exist just to forward an evil notion to destroy credibility and positioning. That's not gonna withstand, because OUR TRUTH is what we experience here daily, backed by YEARS OF GENERALLY A BETTER QUALITY OF LIFE. #davaocity  #raisedbyaduterte   SunStar Davao ,  Davao Today , Ry Llanes,  MindaNews , Kgwd Raymund Carin Gumanid,  GMA Regional TV News Personal Note: Davao is not "better" than other places. text: Dutertes Bring Comfort and Immediate Aid to Flood Evacuees in Bangkal DAVAO CITY – As floodwaters forced families to leave the safety of their homes on Friday evening, First District Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte and Vice Mayor Rodrigo "Rigo" Duterte II moved quickly to ensure that those affected were not left to face the ordeal alone. Continuous heavy rains caused a nearby creek to overflow, sending floodwaters into homes in Barangay Talomo and prompting local authorities to carry out a preemptive evacuation to keep residents safe. Through the Office of the First Congressional District and the Office of the Vice Mayor, immediate relief assistance was delivered to families taking shelter in evacuation centers, providing essential supplies to help them through the difficult night. Understanding that comfort can come from something as simple as a warm meal, Rep. Duterte and Vice Mayor Duterte also organized community cooking activities for evacuees at the Our Lady of Lourdes Central Park Gym and the Bangkal Satellite Gym in Royal Valley. Volunteers prepared and served freshly cooked meals, offering not only nourishment but also a sense of care and solidarity to families temporarily displaced by the flooding.

text: FOR THE NATION, NOT FOR DRAMA To our public servants in Congress: We don't need your tears. We need your receipts. The ₱7.2-trillion budget for 2027 belongs to every Filipino. It belongs to the farmer in Nueva Ecija, the fisherman in Samar, the OFW in Dubai, the jeepney driver in Cebu, and the teacher in Mindanao. It came from our taxes, our sweat, and our sacrifices. So instead of crying in the session hall, hold a press conference and tell the people:  "We approved your budget."  "Here is where every peso goes."  "Here is what your city and province will receive."  "We are ready to serve you in 2027." The House passed the ₱7.2-trillion budget on second reading on October 7, with ₱116 billion in amendments, and the final vote is set for Monday, October 12. Budget watchdogs are already warning that about ₱541.4 billion could go to "pork allocations". That is why the Filipino people are asking: WHERE IS THE MONEY GOING?  DPWH: ₱644 billion. Which roads, bridges and flood controls? Where, and when will they be finished?  Agriculture and agrarian reform: ₱276.57 billion. Will it reach our farmers?  DSWD: ₱241.56 billion. Will it reach the families who need it most? Our call is simple. POST THE BUDGET in every city hall, every provincial capitol and every barangay. Put it online, line by line, project by project. Let every Filipino see, check and monitor where the money goes. Transparency is not a favor. It is our right. Accountability is not optional. It is your duty. We don't pay taxes for tears. We pay for roads, schools, hospitals, jobs and our future. text: Floodwaters rose in Taal, Bangkal, Davao City following the heavy rainfall on the evening of July 24, 2026. Several residents have already been rescued and safely evacuated. If I had one wish, it would be for every kind family, every innocent soul, every beloved pet, and every homeless stray to be kept safe from the flood. And if it must reach somewhere, let it expose the places that have shown cruelty instead, like the impounding facilities where animals are neglected, the establishments that drive away hungry strays, and the homes of owners who abandoned or abused the lives they chose to keep. Because the voiceless deserve mercy. Cruelty does not. My heart is with everyone affected today, especially the voiceless. text: Olongapo City, Zambales  is facing widespread flooding as persistent Southwest Monsoon, or Habagat, rains continue to swell rivers and waterways across the city. According to The Philippine Daily Inquirer, floodwaters overflowed the Sta. Rita and Del Rosario bridges, affecting parts of Sta. Rita, West Bajac-Bajac, East Bajac-Bajac and Kalaklan, while several major roads became impassable. The situation became more serious on August 29, when the Olongapo City Information Center, cited by Inquirer, reported that 1,395 people from 452 families were already staying in evacuation centers, with other residents seeking shelter outside designated facilities. Some communities experienced waist- to neck-deep flooding, while rescue teams were deployed to assist stranded residents. The flooding was driven by continuous monsoon rains, with PAGASA placing Zambales under a Red Rainfall Warning, meaning serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas. Authorities continue to monitor river levels and conduct rescue and evacuation operations as rain persists. For many residents, familiar streets and neighborhoods have temporarily turned into waterways, forcing families to leave their homes and move toward safer ground. The situation remains dangerous, particularly near swollen rivers, bridges and rapidly flowing floodwater, and residents in vulnerable areas are being urged to follow evacuation orders and local disaster warnings. text: NBI Serves Subpoena to DPWH Davao Director Amid Flood Control Probe DAVAO CITY— The National Bureau of Investigation has served a subpoena to DPWH Davao Regional Director Juby Blancaver Cordon as part of its ongoing investigation into alleged anomalies in flood control projects in Davao Region. The subpoena was issued as the NBI looks into reports of irregularities and questionable disbursements tied to flood mitigation works in the area. Investigators said Cordon was required to appear before the bureau and submit documents related to project implementation, bidding, and fund utilization. The probe forms part of a wider scrutiny of flood control spending nationwide following public complaints and reports of substandard or incomplete projects despite large budget allocations.

text: Polk County Weather Update | 11:45 P.M. Hurricane Isaias made landfall along the Gulf Coast earlier this evening and continues to move inland. Residents should be prepared for strong wind gusts, heavy rainfall, downed trees and power lines, scattered to prolonged power outages, localized flooding, and the potential for brief spin-up tornadoes within incoming rain bands. Charge electronic devices, ensure you have flashlights readily available, and have multiple ways to receive weather warnings while you sleep. Do not rely on a single source of information overnight. Polk County Emergency Management continues to monitor conditions around the clock. We will provide updates, warning information, and local impact reports as conditions warrant throughout the overnight hours and into the weekend.

By 7-9 AM, the shower activity will be a little more broken a part, in a traditional tropical squall sense. These will last through the day and as the day wears on, elevate the tornado threat. RIVER/STREAM FLOODING: Watch area creeks and rivers to potentially get into flood stage if a heavier band sets up over its basin. Unfortunately, we can't pinpoint these until its happening. text: TODAY | The BFP Special Rescue Unit, now known as the Special Rescue Force (SRF), marks its 28th year of unwavering service to the Filipino people. From the harrowing operations of the Payatas Tragedy to the devastating SuperFerry 14 bombing, the men and women of the SRF have stood on the frontlines of the nation’s most difficult rescue missions. Clad in their iconic orange—now in pixelated form for greater visibility—the team became a symbol of courage, hope, and relentless commitment amid disaster. Today, that same spirit continues as SRF teams respond to earthquakes, floods, fires, and collapsed structures across the country, including deployments to assist communities affected by major disasters such as the recent earthquake response in Cebu.  For 28 years, through danger, darkness, and uncertainty, the Special Rescue Force has remained a constant—ready to climb higher, dig deeper, and go further to save lives. The SRF will always be visible. The SRF will always answer the call.
